sections.title: Location
sections.body:
Adam can be found in the Doctor Blackbrew's Castle on the western edge of Gloomrot north, above Trancendum Laboratories.

Access to the boss is blocked by a gate and a door. Each can be destroyed for 1 hour by using an . Alternatively, it is possible to fly over the gate using  to save 1 EMP. It is also possible to bypass both obstacles when leaving by getting out through a breach in the wall near the switch and then jumping off the cliff.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
Adam is an incredibly fast and aggressive boss, nearly always being within melee range of the player. This Combined with stage hazards, attacks that cover nearly the entire arena and a second phase make Adam an incredibly difficult fight, especially if fought alone. His attacks are as follow:

*Lightning Towers - The arena which Adam is fought within has eight lightning towers, two on each wall. Towers opposite one another create a continuous stream of lightning that deals damage and slows the player as long as they remain within it. A pair of towers can be deactivated by dealing sufficient damage to one of the towers. Adam will start the fight by activating all towers. Occasionally, Adam will reactivate a pair of towers. He can do this in both phases.

sections.title: Phase 1
sections.body:
*Dash - If the player is too far away from Adam, The Monster will dash towards them. This dash has no other effects other than moving Adam towards the player.
*Slash Combo - Adam will slash in front of himself with his blade-arm, once to his left then once to his right. Each slash releases a rock wave projectile in the direction of the slash, dealing damage to the player. After the slashes, Adam will slam in front of himself, dealing damage in a line. Three rock waves will be launched from the tip of Adam's blade in a cone after he slams.
*Grab - Adam will step forward in an attempt to grab the player. If he succeeds, he will throw the player across the arena, dealing damage and stunning them when they land.
*Stomp - Adam will stomp the ground, dealing damage around himself and releasing rock waves in a fixed pattern around himself.
*Eye of the Storm - Adam will stop to conjure a thunderstorm, knocking nearby players back once he finishes. During the thunderstorm, lightning will strike across the arena, dealing damage to players. Adam will continue to attack normally while the storm is happening.
*Shield - Starting at around 80% health, Adam will quickly shield himself and knockback the player a short distance. While shielded, Adam can't take damage, move or attack. Hitting Adam while the shield persists will cause lightning projectiles to be launched around The Monster in seemingly random patterns.
*Skewer - Starting at around 50% health, Adam will rapidly dash in front of the player then attempt to skewer them. If he's successful, he'll pick up the player and deal damage to them. Afterwards, he'll slam them to the ground beside him, dealing damage again and inflicting a short stun
*No Escape - Starting at around 50% health, Adam will rapidly charge behind the player then slam the ground, affecting the area in a cone in front of himself. If the player is in that area they will take damage, get flung away from Adam and become incapacitated.
*Lightning Field - Starting at around 30% health, Adam will take a moment to create four electric mines around himself initially. Afterwards, the mines will slowly spread across the entire arena, persisting for awhile. The mines will occasionally detonate, dealing damage around themselves without despawning. The player will continuously take damage for as long as they make contact with a mine.

sections.title: Phase 2
sections.body:
After Adam's health is depleted, he will drop down for a moment before breaking his blade-arm, replacing it with a lightning arm and beginning phase 2. During this phase, Adam loses access to his Slash Combo, Skewer, Stomp and No Escape, keeping everything else while gaining new attacks.

*Lightning Swipes - Adam will quickly swipe in front of himself, once to his left then once to his right, releasing lines of electricity as he swipes. Afterwards, Adam will rapidly dash behind the player and slam the ground, doing damage in a straight line in front of himself.
*Helix - If the player is too far away from Adam, he will launch two fast lightning ball projectiles towards them that travel in a double helix pattern. Both projectiles deal damage and incapacitate the player if they connect.
*Death Ray - Adam will take a moment to summon a death ray on top of the player. Shortly after spawning, the death ray will begin doing damage to the player as long as they remain within its area of effect. The death ray will chase after the player and persist through Adam's succeeding attacks.
*Storm Leap - Adam will leap into the air, summoning a thunderstorm as he leaps. As expected, lightning will continuously strike while the thunderstorm rages. Once the thunderstorm finishes, Adam will crash down on top of the player, dealing damage and incapacitating in a large area.

sections.title: Other notes
sections.body:
# Adam's slashes and swipes reach both to his side as well as slightly behind him.
# Adam starts phase two at half health. Due to this, he also doesn't spawn additional healing orbs during this phase.
# The lightning towers can block Adam's projectiles.
# Adam's dash can sometimes make him dash behind the player.
# For Brutal Only: His fight is unchanged except his Lightning Towers. They will start Shielded/Invulnerable until the shield goes down after a set time, which you can take it down, but it will come back shielded and repeat.

sections.title: Equipment and Abilities
sections.body:
Upgraded , and an upgrade of the  is the best equipment for the fight. For weapons, crossbows are very hard to use during the fight due to Adam giving the player little time to fire due to him being so close all the time. However, the player may want to bring a crossbow as a secondary weapon to deal with the lighting towers from further away. Pistols don't run into this problem as much due to their faster firing and shorter range. In fact, pistols as well as greatswords can be great choices to deal with one of Adam's more problematic attack. Whatever weapon the player ends up using, it should be either sanguine or ancestral. 

Hard hitting abilities with good range can be used to destroy the lightning towers and free up space for the player. Counters and blocks have less attacks to defend against due to Adam's very high count of area damage. That said, these defensive abilities are still useful to deal with Adam's melee attacks and should still be considered. 

For ultimates,  's mix of defense and offense works great against Adam who will usually stay within the area of affect of the ultimate willingly, though the player should be careful where they dash when the ability ends.

sections.title: The Fight
sections.body: General Tips: The lightning towers effectively split the arena into an uneven 3x3 grid. Depending on which area you find yourself within, it will become much harder to dodge Adam if you don't deactivate the towers to make room or if you don't dash over the lightning beams to get to a more spacious part. It's advised to spend the beginning of the fight to deactivate most if not all of the towers. After that, the fight becomes more manageable. However, the player should make sure to keep the towers deactivated. If not, the player will find themselves in situations where it  will be incredibly hard to dodge Adam's attacks or even outright impossible to get out of a tough spot without taking damage. Lastly, Adam's attacks that displace or throw the player can be very dangerous while there are still lightning towers active as Adam can force you on top of the beams, often times stunning you on top of them.

sections.title: Phase 1
sections.body:
Slash Combo: The attack can be completely dodged if the player keeps a short distance from Adam then moving to their left (Adam's right) when he performs the first swing, then the opposite direction on the second swing. After which, the player only needs to sidestep the slam as the rock waves will spawn behind the player if they keep close enough to Adam since the waves spawn out of the tip of his blade rather than himself. The player can also avoid this attack by making distance between themselves and Adam as he will not attempt to reposition once he starts the attack at which point the player should focus on dodging the rock waves that follow. Lastly, the player can also dash behind Adam to avoid the attack. However, unlike with other bosses who have attacks dodged this way, Adam can still reach the player with his wide swings, even if he doesn't see you. You should also wait for Adam to start his slam before attacking as he can turn very quickly to hit you. Any attack in this combo can be countered or blocked.

Grab:  The grab can be walked away from and sidestepped, albeit this is rather unreliable. Therefore, the safest way to avoid getting grabbed is using your Travel Ability or other similar effects, such as the second ability of the greatsword or pistols. The grab is Adam's longest stun and will do a lot of damage if he decides to toss you on top of a lightning tower's beam. However, if you do get grabbed and land near a tower, it will take Adam a few seconds to reach you again, time which could be used to deactivate a tower. The grab CANNOT be countered or blocked.

Stomp: Adam's stomp doesn't have an indicator as to where it will deal damage. If the player stands a modest distance away from Adam then the initial stomp will be avoided. If the player isn't sure of the rock wave pattern it is fairly safe to use a counter or block to avoid being hit by them.

Eye of the Storm: The lightning bolts are obvious to dodge. However, the initial cast of this ability can prove dangerous as well depending on your positioning relative to Adam as this can knock you backwards into the beam of lightning towers. As such, keep a distance from Adam by the time he is casting or angle yourself in such way that going straight backwards wouldn't go into a lightning beam in the case that one is nearby.

Shield: Since the shield makes it impossible to interact with Adam directly, the player should start damaging the lightning towers while the shield holds. The player should also be careful if they have any projectile that lingers such as a reaper's second ability as it will trigger the shield to fire bolts once it is applied.

Skewer and No Escape: These two attacks are being addressed at once because of the fact that they can be easily confused with one another. Avoiding this generally comes down to reaction time due to the speed Adam performs the attacks. Generally speaking, dashing backwards or using similar effects will dodge both attacks. As for specifics, Skewer can sometimes be sidestepped but it can also be countered or blocked, while No Escape can be dodged by walking towards Adam and slightly to the side after he dashes behind you.

phases.body:

If, however, you have no such effects, DO NOT use your dash during the thunderstorm even if it means getting hit by a lightning strike as you will not have it back up in time and Adam crashing down does more damage. However, for this attack specifically,   could be a good choice to give you at least one dash before Adam crashes down.

entities.title: Albert the Duke of Balaton
entities.description: The patriarch of a family that once held land when these swamps were adequately inhabited. Over time, the cursed land twisted them, leaving this horrible, twisted toad that only remembers its lust for gold and jewels. It jealously guards its hoard of forgotten, worthless currency.

entities.title: Alpha the White Wolf
entities.description: The trail of this scent bears the unmistakable signature of Dracula, the Immortal King. When Dracula fell, he cursed the world of Vardoran with a blood rain, a scourge in which many perished. Some who survived became unknowingly twisted by the downpour, their bloodlines forever empowered by his malice. This mighty predator is infused with that legacy.

sections.title: Location
sections.body: Alpha Wolf can be found roaming the roads of the Farbane Woods region. It tends to walk along the roads in a circuit around the central part of the region, near the [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=81 Wolf Den]. It will often cross paths with and fight Lidia the Chaos Archer and Goreswine the Ravager. It will also fight any Bandit or Undead enemy that crosses its path.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
*Bite - Standard melee attack.
*Lunge - The Alpha Wolf will crouch down for a second in preparation and then launch itself forward in a straight line.
*Rage - The Alpha Wolf howls and glows red, launch itself in a straight line and bite 2 times.
*Summon Minions - The Alpha Wolf stops for a moment, howls, and summons 2 regular wolves to join the fight.

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty
sections.body: *Pounce  - During the Rage phase, the Alpha Wolf pounces on and stuns the player while biting them multiple times (similarly to the Slaughterbeast).

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
Alpha Wolf is the first V blood carrier, as a result this fight is fairly simple and can be tackled as long as the player has been following the quests. Like other roaming V Blood Carriers, it is possible to kite either Alpha Wolf or roaming bandits into a fight against each other leaving you to mop up the weakened victor. Be mindful that if a mob is kited too far from the initial point of aggro, they will disengage and return to that point of aggro, this is true even mid fight.

An alternative strategy is to setup your base and mine some Copper Nodes within Farbane Woods to then craft a Copper Weapon which will make you overpowered for this fight and able to take on the next couple of Vblood carriers straight away (this method may in fact increase efficiency if you are trying to get through the starting area quickly).

entities.title: Angram the Purifier
entities.description: A dedicated servant of the Trancendum, Angram was an exterminator that possessed a natural cruelty and resilence unmatched by any of his peers. Like any good soldier, he gave his life for his cause... or tried to, anyway. Doctor Henry Blackbrew could not let such an asset go to waste and brought him back to life with a brutal surgery few other beings could survive. Angram lives now, at the mere cost of every last scrap of his humanity.

entities.title: Bane the Shadowblade
entities.description: Once a formidable swordsman and legendary graverobber, Bane was caught by the Cult of the Damned during one of his many heists. Seeing the benefit of his talent for infiltration, instead of killing him, they corrupted him into a servant of undeath. It's said that his clandestine abilities were crucial in the capture and corruption of the Iron Mine over the Militia.

sections.title: Location
sections.body:
Bane can be found roaming the roads of Dunley Farmlands, disguised as a human.

He only fights when he is attacked. People attack him as soon as his camouflage ends. It can make the fight easier if guards attack with you.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
*Triple Slash - He will slash at you three times. Third attack is a lunge which will incapacitate you.
*Triple Knife Throw - He will dash away from you and throw three knives at you.
*Dark Spin - His phrases will be all about Darkness or Black magic, He will do a purple AoE slash that surrounds him.
*Teleport Strike - He will teleport out of view and reappear near you to strike, which will incapacitate you.
*Into the Shadows - He will say one of his few phrases emphasizing he will disappear, but will summon a multitude of cloaked figures (much like when you hit him to start the fight), he will be one of them, damaging one that is not him will summon Skeletal Warrior and Undead Assassins.
*Shadow Clone - At less then 50% health, his dash from the knife throw will leave a lingering shadow which will also throw knives at you.
*Brutal and Incursion Rift: His Knife attack can be chained multiple times in a row. For Incursion only, his Into the Shadow move will have an aura above him, but the minions spawned are Draculin mobs.

sections.title: Trivia
sections.body: Bane will attack wandering bosses if provoked near them. This might prove helpful if the player have troubles dealing with some of the Dunley wandering bosses. He will make short work of Vincent the Frostbringer, giving the player access to the Prison Cells early, and is able to kill Jade the Vampire Hunter if there's not too many regular enemies around. Fighting Jade will leave him quite damaged so the player might try to finish Bane off afterwards.

entities.title: Baron du Bouchon the Sommelier
entities.description: Formerly a traveling swordsman-for-hire, the good baron earned his title of Grand Sommelier after winning a taste contest hosted by the Church of Luminance. His abilities were so extraordinary, it's said that he can name the ingredients, their ages, and their place of origin with only a sip of brew. Though his new position offers him all the worldly goods he could desire, those who know him well suspect he may miss the taste of blood on the tip of his blade most of all.

sections.title: Location
sections.body: Beatrice can be found in the [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=73 Dawnbreak Village] in the South-East of Dunley Farmlands.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
Beatrice runs away from the player and attracts enemies in a similar way to a Bell Ringer.
* No Attacks

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty
sections.body:
Beatrice will not attack in her first phase, and will instead run away and attract enemies similarly to normal difficulty. However, after the player gets her to 50% health, a demonic red circle will appear around her and she will morph into a Gargoyle wearing a shawl, and heal for around 25% of her health. She has the same attacks as a regular Gargoyle:
*Double Slice - She dashes and slices at the nearest player twice.
*Front Leap - She leaps towards the nearest player, landing in an AoE on the ground.
*Chaotic Landing - She flies into the air and after a couple seconds delay crashes down above the farthest player leaving an AoE that deals  damage.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
On normal difficulty, Beatrice will run away from the player when attacked and will call out for help to attract other enemies. She does not have any attacks and the fight is entirely focused around clearing the Militia enemies while chasing her. It is common for Beatrice to run into groups of other mobs causing the player to become overwhelmed if she is not killed quickly so using abilities that limit enemy movement may be useful in this hunt. Anything that slows her down (e.g. Ice spells or stuns) or knocks her back will be helpful to keep her in place once you've managed to corner her by a wall or inside of a house. You can also use the Harpoon special attack of an Iron grade or higher spear to reel her back towards you. 

On Brutal difficulty, the same applies until Beatrice reaches 50% HP, whereupon she transforms into a gargoyle. At this point, any Militia guards will attack her instead of defending her and she will attack them in turn. Her gargoyle forms deals high damage but has no ranged abilities beyond its leaps and can therefore be kited and damaged with ranged weapons and spells.

On normal difficulty, the best choice for attacking her is to fully clear the village of all other enemies before killing her. This is mostly the same on Brutal, with the caveat that keeping some Militia guards alive in one corner of the village can be useful for distracting her Gargoyle form.

Two other V Bloods, Christina the Sun Priestess and Jade the Vampire Hunter, will occasionally patrol through Dawnbreak Village and come to Beatrice's defense if she's being attacked in human form. However, if she's in gargoyle form then they will attack her instead. If the player has unlocked the ability to track these V Bloods then they should check how close they are to the village before starting a fight.

sections.title: Location
sections.body: Christina can be found traveling between the churches of [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=113 Mosswick Village] and [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=89 Dawnbreak Village]. She can usually be found roaming the southern roads of Dunley Farmlands, accompanied by 2 Militia Guards.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
* Staff Swipe - If the player or a minion is in melee range of her, she raises her staff and swings it in a medium arc in front of her after a brief delay.
* Holy Rays - She aims her staff like a gun, before firing 5 fast-moving holy missiles in a fan in front of her.
* Holy Wrath - She plants her staff in the ground and calls down an AoE beacon of holy light upon the player's position after a brief delay. The AoE slows the player's movement before exploding after a couple seconds delay.
* Shining Blessings - After she has lost health, she occasionally shouts "Shining Blessings!", raises her staff in the air, and becomes stationary while slowly healing herself. She cannot use any other abilities while channeling this one. Abilities which stun enemies (such as the Iron tier and higher Axes' X-Strike ability) will interrupt her healing.
* Conviction Counter - If the player is close to her, she shouts "This is my conviction!", surrounding herself in Holy light and counters all incoming attacks. Anyone who hits this counter will be silenced for several seconds.
* Summon Militia - She shouts "I will show you discipline!" and summons a Militia Crossbowman and Militia Guard to come to her defense.

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty
sections.body:
* Holy Rays - She now fires 7 Holy projectiles instead of 5.
* Holy Wrath - This ability now heals any of her allies who stand in its explosion.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
The focus of this fight is on disrupting Christina's healing and killing her allies so that the player can keep their full attention on her. Area of effect spells such as  or  can kill her minions quickly while barrier spells such as  or  will protect the player from her Holy Rays projectiles. Any ability with a stun should be saved to cancel her Shining Blessings, with the aforementioned Iron Axes being an easy way to accomplish this. 

All of Christina's damage is Holy damage, so raising your Holy resistance via a Holy Resistance Potion will reduce her damage and make this fight easier. These potions can occasionally be found in chests around Dunley or crafted after defeating Meredith the Bright Archer (who frequently dies to Kriig the Undead General).

Christina's patrol route will occasionally cause her to cross paths with other V Bloods who will come to her defense, such as Vincent the Frostbringer and Jade the Vampire Hunter. She will also be joined in battle by any Militia guards who pass by. Baiting her to follow you into a field or vacant plot will help minimize the chance of allies coming to her aid.

"It seems you need to be taught a lesson- like any child!"

"In the name of Luminance, you must be purged!"

"I will do as the Light demands me!"

sections.body:
"I did everything I could."

"...Is THIS my reward?!"

"There is still time... to repent..."

"Our time... must come. Take me, Light!"

"Light, bring me salvation..."

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
*Cluster Bomb - He throws a bomb in the air which explodes and splits into 3 more bombs, then explodes again and splits into 9 bombs.
*Time Bomb - He drops a large bomb at his feet with a large explosion radius that takes a couple seconds to explode.

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty
sections.body:
*Sticky Bomb - He throws a fast-moving projectile that, if it hits a player, will cause a timer to appear underneath them along with the words "Sticky Bomb", which will explode when the timer runs out.  The thrown sticky bomb can be blocked with a counter but the explosion if it sticks to you cannot. Time your Veil with the detonation to avoid taking damage while you're immaterial.
**Clive will throw another Sticky Bomb right as the first is about to explode. With proper timing, it is possible to avoid both Sticky Bombs with one Veil dash.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
Make sure to clear the area of Bandits before engaging Clive. The Explosive boxes nearby can either be safely detonated so the player doesn't have to worry about them during the fight, or left standing so that the player can potentially damage Clive with them.

Clive is most easily dealt with using a ranged weapon or spells, since that will allow the player to more easily sidestep his bombs while still dealing consistent damage to him.

On Brutal difficulty, it is essential to save your Veil dash in case Clive hits you with a Sticky Bomb. Without your Veil you will be forced to take a large amount of damage and may even get hit with a follow-up Sticky Bomb if you're not careful. Fighting him in melee range is also much more difficult here since his sticky bomb can hit you instantly if you're right in front of him when he throws it.

Cyril himself has access to an arsenal of weapons, each with a specific ability. He can also forge spectral weapons, which cast their abilities shortly after Cyril casts the ability of the same weapon.

*Sword - Dash forward, then cleave
*Spear - Dash backward, then throw a piercing spear
*Mace - Levitate, then slam down and create spheres in a ring around the caster, spirally traveling outward.

*Create weapon - Cyril creates a new spectral weapon to fight alongside him.

entities.description: Dantos is a master of weapons, fascinated by both their construction and application. A true obsessive, his borderline inhuman dedication to his craft made him an excellent tool for his Queen, the great witch Megara. entities.title: Dracula the Immortal King
entities.description:
When Dracula fell centuries ago, it seemed like the Church of Luminance had done the impossible. The death of the Immortal King. However, in his final moments, Dracula enacted his final gambit and cast a cloud over Vardoran. The blood rain that followed would plant the seeds of Dracula’s will across the realm, twisting it, and filling it with his storied essence. 

After death, the Immortal King’s soul was cast out to where his otherworldly powers originated, the Shadow Realm. There he lingered, biding his time. Now the time has come. Dracula floods the world with his monstrous Legion of Noctum, having them gather the blood necessary for him to become whole once more and return to Vardoran.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
*Teleport - Whenever the Player is out his reach, he will teleport and do his stab, slash, or axe attack.
*Wolf Rush - He will transform into a wolf and rush behind you and will slash at you.
*Crimson Slasher - He will swing his sword vertically twice shooting beams from right to left.
*Dread Stab - He will teleport and Stab you with his sword, which will also Incapacitate you.
*Blood Wave - He will stab his sword into the ground causing six beams to rush out.
*Howling Axes - He will teleport away from you in one of the corners of the arena to throw two axes that circle towards you and then back to Dracula. They can be blocked by a pillar or ward.  They may change course dramatically if Dracula uses a teleport while they are in flight.
*Crimson Bats - Will use this move at 75%, often paired with his Teleport.
*Bloody Spiral - Dracula begins shooting out a spiral of blood bolts in 3 directions at once.  Meanwhile a ring closes in on you.  If you remain in the ring its whole duration you will be stunned and then hit backwards.
*Writhing Crimson Night - He will teleport out of view, darken your screen and summon crimson bats that will partial predict your movement, which can be destroyed, blocked or dodged. Afterwards he will reappear near you summoning a circle and if in too long, will grab you and drain some of your Blood, throw you and Stun you.
*Vampiric Curse -  A status effect that will be inflicted if you are hit by most of his attacks. Has no direct effect, but after the timer runs out an explosion will occur with its centre at the location of the player. This can damage your fellow vampires except for Dracula himself. The damage can be dodged however if you are immaterial during the explosion from veil, mist trance or abilities with such effects. (Note: Vampiric Curse effect does not apply if there is only one person fighting him)
*Blood Wave MKII - 2nd Phase version of Blood wave, functions the same, but at the end of the waves span will spawn blood pools which will explode.
*Crimson Slasher MKII - 2nd Phase version of Crimson Slasher, but will send 2 more beams following the pattern.
*Blood Crystal - 2nd Phase move. He will beckon at you and wave his hand to summon a Crystal. The crystal will circle around the arena projecting an aura, touching said aura will damage you. Can be destroyed. He may do this multiple times.
*Blood Sword Rain - 2nd Phase Attack. He will summon swords that rain down on you, with small area of effect.
*Nightstalker Clone - Phase 2 attack. He will summon a visibly shadowy clone of himself to do his Dread leap. Can be ignored or destroyed.
*Dread Leap - He will jump at you with his sword extended outward.
*Bloody Cross - 2nd Phase move. He will teleport to the center of the arena with an indicator of a cross pattern, he will summon crimson flames and will shoot partial predicted blood bolts at your location. Dodge or ward the blood bolts.
*Blood Bolt Wall - 2nd Phase move. He will teleport, stand still and shoot a wall of blood bolts. Center often empty, or you can dodge or ward.
*Brutal Only- Blood Vortex- At the start of Phase 4, Dracula will summon a encroaching Blood vortex, the radius shrinks until there is very little walk space. It does continuous damage while standing in it.
*Brutal Only- Shockwave - During his 4th phase as the blood vortex shrinks, he will do a shockwave move (does no damage, like Henry Blackbrew the Doctor) to push you into the vortex.

sections.title: Phase 1
sections.body:
During Dracula's first phase focus on avoiding damage.  Veil behind the wolf after it jumps over you, counter the axes, avoid blood waves by either getting behind Dracula or keeping your distance, sidestep sword attacks.  When the screen goes dark, save your veil to dodge the grab at the end.

Once he drops to about 55% health, he will fly to the center of the arena and enter his second phase.  Use this time to heal or revive downed allies.

sections.title: Phase 2
sections.body: During Dracula's second phase, he will teleport to the center of the arena and become invulnerable while destroying the pillars.  When he lands he will immediately summon a Blood Crystal, and then use his various phase 2 moves.  He will no longer use Wolf Rush or Howling Axes.

sections.title: Phase 3 (Brutal Only)
sections.body:
During Dracula's third phase he will slowly regenerate his health while he spawns blood souls to boost his heal (+500 health per soul). Your objective is to kill them before they reach Dracula.  Eventually he will spawn the Heart of Dracula. Damage and feed on it to change your Blood Type to Blood of the Immortal with the following effects (will return to your previous type after the battle):
* Increased Physical Power and Spell Power
* Increased Movement Speed &  Increased Primary Attack Speed
* Damage Reduction.
* Increased Veil Cooldown Rate.
* Increased Spell and Weapon Charge Gain.

sections.title: Phase 4 (Brutal Only)
sections.body: During Dracula's final phase he will channel a blood storm blocking part of the arena and only leaving a small radius (It get smaller as time goes on) with himself at the center. He will use his sword rain but the damage area is much bigger. Plus he will use his blood bolt wall ability every few seconds and release shockwaves to try to knock you into the blood storm (It hurts really bad).

combat.fightGuide:
Teleport - Whenever the Player is out his reach, he will teleport and do his stab, slash, or axe attack.
Wolf Rush - He will transform into a wolf and rush behind you and will slash at you.
Crimson Slasher - He will swing his sword vertically twice shooting beams from right to left.
Dread Stab - He will teleport and Stab you with his sword, which will also Incapacitate you.
Blood Wave - He will stab his sword into the ground causing six beams to rush out.
Howling Axes - He will teleport away from you in one of the corners of the arena to throw two axes that circle towards you and then back to Dracula. They can be blocked by a pillar or ward.  They may change course dramatically if Dracula uses a teleport while they are in flight.
Crimson Bats - Will use this move at 75%, often paired with his Teleport.
Bloody Spiral - Dracula begins shooting out a spiral of blood bolts in 3 directions at once.  Meanwhile a ring closes in on you.  If you remain in the ring its whole duration you will be stunned and then hit backwards.
Writhing Crimson Night - He will teleport out of view, darken your screen and summon crimson bats that will partial predict your movement, which can be destroyed, blocked or dodged. Afterwards he will reappear near you summoning a circle and if in too long, will grab you and drain some of your Blood, throw you and Stun you.
Vampiric Curse -  A status effect that will be inflicted if you are hit by most of his attacks. Has no direct effect, but after the timer runs out an explosion will occur with its centre at the location of the player. This can damage your fellow vampires except for Dracula himself. The damage can be dodged however if you are immaterial during the explosion from veil, mist trance or abilities with such effects. (Note: Vampiric Curse effect does not apply if there is only one person fighting him)
Blood Wave MKII - 2nd Phase version of Blood wave, functions the same, but at the end of the waves span will spawn blood pools which will explode.
Crimson Slasher MKII - 2nd Phase version of Crimson Slasher, but will send 2 more beams following the pattern.
Blood Crystal - 2nd Phase move. He will beckon at you and wave his hand to summon a Crystal. The crystal will circle around the arena projecting an aura, touching said aura will damage you. Can be destroyed. He may do this multiple times.
Blood Sword Rain - 2nd Phase Attack. He will summon swords that rain down on you, with small area of effect.
Nightstalker Clone - Phase 2 attack. He will summon a visibly shadowy clone of himself to do his Dread leap. Can be ignored or destroyed.
Dread Leap - He will jump at you with his sword extended outward.
Bloody Cross - 2nd Phase move. He will teleport to the center of the arena with an indicator of a cross pattern, he will summon crimson flames and will shoot partial predicted blood bolts at your location. Dodge or ward the blood bolts.
Blood Bolt Wall - 2nd Phase move. He will teleport, stand still and shoot a wall of blood bolts. Center often empty, or you can dodge or ward.
Brutal Only- Blood Vortex- At the start of Phase 4, Dracula will summon a encroaching Blood vortex, the radius shrinks until there is very little walk space. It does continuous damage while standing in it.
Brutal Only- Shockwave - During his 4th phase as the blood vortex shrinks, he will do a shockwave move (does no damage, like Henry Blackbrew the Doctor) to push you into the vortex.

phases.title: Phase 1
phases.body:
During Dracula's first phase focus on avoiding damage.  Veil behind the wolf after it jumps over you, counter the axes, avoid blood waves by either getting behind Dracula or keeping your distance, sidestep sword attacks.  When the screen goes dark, save your veil to dodge the grab at the end.
Once he drops to about 55% health, he will fly to the center of the arena and enter his second phase.  Use this time to heal or revive downed allies.

phases.title: Phase 2
phases.body: During Dracula's second phase, he will teleport to the center of the arena and become invulnerable while destroying the pillars.  When he lands he will immediately summon a Blood Crystal, and then use his various phase 2 moves.  He will no longer use Wolf Rush or Howling Axes.

phases.title: Phase 3 (Brutal Only)
phases.body:
During Dracula's third phase he will slowly regenerate his health while he spawns blood souls to boost his heal (+500 health per soul). Your objective is to kill them before they reach Dracula.  Eventually he will spawn the Heart of Dracula. Damage and feed on it to change your Blood Type to Blood of the Immortal with the following effects (will return to your previous type after the battle):
Increased Physical Power and Spell Power
Increased Movement Speed &  Increased Primary Attack Speed
Damage Reduction.
Increased Veil Cooldown Rate.
Increased Spell and Weapon Charge Gain.

phases.title: Phase 4 (Brutal Only)
phases.body: During Dracula's final phase he will channel a blood storm blocking part of the arena and only leaving a small radius (It get smaller as time goes on) with himself at the center. He will use his sword rain but the damage area is much bigger. Plus he will use his blood bolt wall ability every few seconds and release shockwaves to try to knock you into the blood storm (It hurts really bad).

entities.title: Errol the Stonebreaker
entities.description: A brutal mining foreman, just as adept at crushing stone as he is crushing bone. Not even his incredible eye for recovering and refining metals was enough to stop him from getting run out of civilised society. His violent rage makes a fine motivator for the miners.

sections.title: Location
sections.body: Errol can be found deep inside the [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=63 Bandit Copper Mine] in central Farbane Woods.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
Errol initially has 3 attacks:
*Aftershock - At long range, he slams the ground creating a shock wave that explodes in a couple seconds.
*Uppercut - At short range, he runs at the player with an uppercut swing.
*Knockback - At short range, he does a spin attack that knocks the player back.

At half health he'll gain 2 additional attacks:
*Summon Minions - He whistles to summon 2 Miners.
*Earthquake - When he shouts "Lets hear that crunch!" he slams the ground creating 4 shock waves that explode in every direction.

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty
sections.body: *Earthquake is upgraded to create 6 shock waves instead of 4.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
Errol only has 3 moves if the player attacks him from long range, making it very easy to predict him while attacking with ranged weapons and spells.

It is advised to clear out the Miners around the area before engaging him.

sections.title: Sighting an enemy
sections.body:
"Hate to break it to you, but your days are numbered!"

"If you want this ore, you're going to have to get through me first!."

"Looks like break time!"

"Hah, I'll handle you myself!"

sections.title: Death
sections.body:
"Crush me."

"Feels... heavy."

"Think I broke something."

"I think I overworked myself."

"Guess it's time to take that break."

entities.title: Finn the Fisherman
entities.description: Finn is a legendary fisherman who hails from the rocky shores of Silverlight Hills. Caught fishing in the Church of Luminance's "sacred" waters, he was set to be executed by live burial at sea. The fisherman emerged from the depths, mysterious and miraculously alive, and went into hiding in the safety of the lawless lands of the Farbane Woods.

sections.title: Location
sections.body: Finn can be found at the Fishing Lake near the Hallowed Mountains in the northeastern corner of Farbane Woods.

sections.title: Dynamic Clouds
sections.body: His arena has dynamic clouds that appear during Daytime.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
*Fish slap: A two hit combo where he slaps the player with a fish, then follows up with a kick.
*Tornado: Winds up before performing a spin attack with his fishing pole that deals damage and knocks the player back.
*Throw Net: Much like the Trapper ability, Finn swings a net around before throwing it into the AoE indicator. Players still in that zone when he throws the net will be pulled to Finn's location and briefly prevented from moving. Additionally, any piranhas and pufferfish hit by the attack are also pulled and can hit the player.
*Summon Piranhas: Summons 3 Hungry Piranha enemies, which slowly chase the player while attempting to use a rapidly hitting melee attack.
*Summon Pufferfish: Summons 3 Pufferfish enemies which deal damage and apply  to any player they touch. Dealing any damage to a Pufferfish will cause it to be knocked away. If a Pufferfish is knocked into Finn, it will be killed and Finn will be briefly stunned. If a Pufferfish is killed by any other means it will fire 10 chilling projectiles in every direction around it.
*Summon Serpent: Summons a Young Sea Serpent with a melee bite attack and ranged attack that launches 3 ice projectiles in a fan pattern and applies . Finn may use this attack multiple times if the fight lasts long enough, even if the first serpent is not killed.

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty
sections.body: *Summon Serpent: In Brutal difficulty, this mob is significantly larger and its bite creates a field of ice in a straight line that applies . Its ranged attack also fires 4 AoE ice projectiles instead of 3 ice projectiles in a fan pattern.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
This fight is all about managing Finn's many summons. Area of effect abilities and movement abilities are important for allowing the player to deal with the summons while also keeping up with Finn. However, players should avoid killing the pufferfish and instead try to push them into Finn to stun him. 

On Brutal difficulty, the Young Sea Serpent becomes a massive threat due to its strong AoE attacks requiring constant dodging and sidestepping. Having a weapon that provides additional maneuverability (such as the Axe or Mace) can help with this. The serpent's high health makes it relatively difficult to kill quickly so players may be better off dodging it while focusing all their damage on Finn.

sections.title: Sighting an enemy
sections.body:
"I've been discovered! But you won't take me alive!"

"Who are you? Get away from me, let me be!"

"Get your own watering hole! No trespassers!"

sections.title: Death
sections.body:
"I hope death is more peaceful than this life..."

"Let the waters take me deep!"

"Bury me at sea!"

"Take me to the shore one last time!"

entities.description: Gaius was a skilled militia captain and a famous gladiator. Annoyed at Gaius' popularity competing with his own, as well as that of the Church of Luminance, Raziel arranged for his defeat by way of a cursed blade. entities.title: General Valencia the Depraved
entities.description: Valencia was once a human baroness, part of an affluent noble family from before the great war. Always hungry for power, ambitious, and utterly without moral tethers, she saw the rise of Dracula and his legions as an opportunity to surpass her human limitations and become something greater. Impressed with her utter depravity, Dracula granted the baroness’ wish. Valencia now serves as a vicious general of the Legion of Noctum.

sections.title: Location
sections.body: Valencia can be found in the [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=86 North Fortress Ruins] in Ruins of Mortium.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
*A Thousand Spears - Valencia dashes backwards and thrusts her spears forward in a cone multiple times, not giving the player a chance to cast spells, dash, or attack. She always initiates the fight with this attack. She does this attack if you're close by after summoning Bloody Iron Maiden or being spit out by it.
*Spear Throw - She throws a single spear that pulls the player in. She does this attack if you're far away after summoning Bloody Iron Maiden or being spit out by it.
*Bloody Iron Maiden - At the 75% max health threshhold, she will place an Iron Maiden in the Center of the arena, which if near will drain 25% of your Blood Pool. Spins around slowly to face the player, and shoots out spears that pull the player in at range. Up close it will try to capture the player, dealing damage and stunning upon being spit out. Can be destroyed.
*Thrust Kick - She will glow red, and sprint behind the player and attempt to kick you into the Iron Maiden. Only happens while the Iron Maiden is active.
*Spear Hail - Valencia either dashes backwards a small distance or leaps a great distance away, before throwing many spears into the air and they crash down, creating small craters. Can happen at any point after the first Iron Maiden has been summoned.
*Spear Spin - Valencia spins her spears back and forth, damaging players who touch it and negating all damage from in front of her.

sections.title: Brutal Mode
sections.body: Valencia does not have any new move sets in Brutal mode, but she might be more intelligent about her ability usage.

sections.title: Death
sections.body:
"Thank you for this beautiful death. Until next time."

"Our dance concludes for now, let ours paths cross again."

"Your victory is noted, but remember, darkness is a patient ally."

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
*Swipes - Gorecrusher will prepare before performing two wide swings followed by a thrust with his club arm. 
*Slam Combo - Gorecrusher will let out a roar and begin to glow with Illusion magic before slamming down his club three times, once to his right then once to his left before slamming it straight ahead. Each of the slams stun the player if they connect. 
*Charge - Gorecrusher will prepare to charge a short distance. If the player is hit by the charge they will be flipped a long distance backwards and stunned. 
*Ground slam - Gorecrusher will raise both his arms as a damage circle appears in front of him. When the circle fills up he will slam the ground, doing damage and knocking back the player if they are in the circle, as well as sending out 5 lines of shockwaves in random directions. 
*Leap - If the player gets too far away from Gorecrusher, the Behemoth will leap at the player, signaled by a damage circle filling up. Gorecrusher will not leap if he's performing a charge attack.
*Charge Combo - At about 80% health, Gorecrusher will gain the ability to do 3 long range, non-stunning charges one after the other. Every charge will be delayed and they all will attempt to target ahead of where the player is moving rather than where the player is currently in an attempt to intercept them.
*Illusionary Summons - At about 70% health, Gorecrusher will jump away from the player (while unlikely, his jump away from the player can still deal damage to them if he lands on them). Afterwards, he will summon an illusionary wolf and illusionary bear to attack the player while also apply a warping effect to the screen similar to the Trippy Shroom for 15 seconds, during which time he is also immune. The illusionary animals will act similarly to their standard counterparts and will linger in the fight until they die and will not drop anything. Once Gorecrusher's immunity ends he will run up to the player before quickly slamming down with his club, stunning the player if it connects.
*Wisp Dance - At about 50% health, Gorecrusher will roar, slowing the player and casting a very powerful version of Wisp Dance which will summon a large amount of wisps from his very center. The wisps will linger on the field for a long time and, if they come into contact with the player, will deal damage and apply weaken , reducing their damage and movement speed.
*Soul - At about 30% health, Gorecrusher will stop to roar and knockback the player, summoning a Gorecrusher Soul in the process which is essentially an illusionary clone of himself. The clone is able to perform all of Gorecrusher's attacks independently of the real one except for his leap, his Wisp Dance and Illusionary summons. If the soul would die it will instead drop down becoming immune and will stop attacking while it regenerates. The soul will resume attacking once it reaches half health and the only way to kill the soul for good is killing Gorecrusher himself.

sections.title: Other notes
sections.body:
#If the player becomes hidden through effects such as Veil of Blood while Gorecrusher or his Soul is preparing his slam combo, the boss will not begin slamming until the player is revealed. This can be circumvented by using these effects in the window between the boss roaring and performing the attack.
#When performing his charge combo, Gorecrusher will attempt to charge at the player's last known location if the player becomes hidden. This can be easily seen with Travel Abilities that hide the player.
#While Gorecrusher himself isn't active when he summons the illusionary animals, the Gorecrusher Soul is active during this time.
#Gorecrusher and his Soul can begin an attack in the middle of another attack if the first attack is delayed, causing the first attack to be cancelled in the process.
#The Gorecrusher Soul has considerably less health than the real Gorecrusher.

sections.title: Equipment and Abilities
sections.body: It is advised for the player to use the Bloodmoon Armour set for this fight alongside their choice of Blood Merlot Amulet upgrade and blood type, based on their preferred playstyle. As for abilities, Sanguine Coil can aid the player greatly due to its reliable healing off-sets the fight's more chaotic moments, while Mist Trance can be used to dodge Gorecrusher's stunning attacks while also repositioning. Blocking abilities such as Ward of the Damned can fill a similar role.

sections.title: The Fight
sections.body:
General Tips: When attempting to defeat Gorecrusher, the player has to be very careful with how far away from Gorecrusher they are at all times. In general, Gorecrusher's attacks reward the player being aggressive, most easily seen with his Ground Slam which is at it's easiest to dodge if the player was already standing near the boss, although the player still needs to be careful of the shockwave lines. Consistently staying behind Gorecrusher is also a great way of staying out of danger. With all that said, it isn't impossible to deal damage to Gorecrusher from a safer distance, though the player should be careful when doing so as straying too far away will cause Gorecrusher to leap at them. It should also be noted that the only attacks that can't be countered or blocked during this fight are Gorecrusher's Ground Slam, his Leap and the illusionary bear's Ground Slam.

Swipes and Slam Combos: If the player gets behind Gorecrusher after he starts performing these attacks they will not only be safe from harm but can freely swing at him with their weapon. The player can also attempt to simply walk away from Gorecrusher when he performs these attacks, although it isn't as reliable.

Charge: While this attack can be easily side-stepped, it is much safer to dodge it using your Travel Ability.

Ground Slam and Leap: When Gorecrusher performs these attacks he will always be on the edge of their respective circles rather than in the middle of them. This makes it so that staying near Gorecrusher during the Ground Slam or running towards where he was before leaping is the safest way to deal with these attacks. It's also worth noting that, in the event of the player being unable to get out of the circle in time, it is still possible to avoid taking damage if you time your Travel Ability at the right time.

Charge Combo: While this attack may be seemingly very difficult to dodge, the player can dodge every charge by simply walking. To do this, move left to right while Gorecrusher is preparing to charge, which is when he raises his head. While he is lowering his head, move in the opposite direction of where you were moving previously then repeat this process until he stops charging.

Illusionary Summons: At this point, the player should be familiar with how to fight wolves and bears. The problem of this attack comes when the summons interfere with you trying to dodge Gorecrusher's attacks after he stops being immune. As such, killing the summons during the 15 seconds should be the priority. If this can't be done, heavily injuring them and killing them after is the best course of action. The player should also be mindful of the fast attack that Gorecrusher performs right after becoming vulnerable to damage again and should save their Travel Ability or any defensive ability such as a Counter or Bulwark in order to not take damage.

Wisp Dance: The player should be very careful when Gorecrusher gains this attack as the boss will not push the player back when performing this attack, making it possible to get hit by a lot of the wisps when it is first performed. To circumvent the aftermath of the wisps spawning, the player should get as far away from where they spawned as possible, even if it means making Gorecrusher leap at them.

Gorecrusher Soul: At this point, the fight will become extremely chaotic and a misstep will cause the player to lose a large amount of health as one Gorecrusher is able to stun you while the other prepares another attack. Killing the soul is advisable to make the fight more manageable due to how frail it is. A good way of softening up the soul while also damaging Gorecrusher is using an Ultimate Ability such as Arctic Leap or Mirror Strike. After the first time the soul is killed it will become easier to do so again as it always revives with only half it's health. Although risky, once Gorecrusher is nearly dead, it is worth considering to ignore the soul completely in the hopes of finishing the fight.

combat.fightGuide:
Swipes - Gorecrusher will prepare before performing two wide swings followed by a thrust with his club arm. 
Slam Combo - Gorecrusher will let out a roar and begin to glow with Illusion magic before slamming down his club three times, once to his right then once to his left before slamming it straight ahead. Each of the slams stun the player if they connect. 
Charge - Gorecrusher will prepare to charge a short distance. If the player is hit by the charge they will be flipped a long distance backwards and stunned. 
Ground slam - Gorecrusher will raise both his arms as a damage circle appears in front of him. When the circle fills up he will slam the ground, doing damage and knocking back the player if they are in the circle, as well as sending out 5 lines of shockwaves in random directions. 
Leap - If the player gets too far away from Gorecrusher, the Behemoth will leap at the player, signaled by a damage circle filling up. Gorecrusher will not leap if he's performing a charge attack.
Charge Combo - At about 80% health, Gorecrusher will gain the ability to do 3 long range, non-stunning charges one after the other. Every charge will be delayed and they all will attempt to target ahead of where the player is moving rather than where the player is currently in an attempt to intercept them.
Illusionary Summons - At about 70% health, Gorecrusher will jump away from the player (while unlikely, his jump away from the player can still deal damage to them if he lands on them). Afterwards, he will summon an illusionary wolf and illusionary bear to attack the player while also apply a warping effect to the screen similar to the Trippy Shroom for 15 seconds, during which time he is also immune. The illusionary animals will act similarly to their standard counterparts and will linger in the fight until they die and will not drop anything. Once Gorecrusher's immunity ends he will run up to the player before quickly slamming down with his club, stunning the player if it connects.
Wisp Dance - At about 50% health, Gorecrusher will roar, slowing the player and casting a very powerful version of Wisp Dance which will summon a large amount of wisps from his very center. The wisps will linger on the field for a long time and, if they come into contact with the player, will deal damage and apply weaken , reducing their damage and movement speed.
Soul - At about 30% health, Gorecrusher will stop to roar and knockback the player, summoning a Gorecrusher Soul in the process which is essentially an illusionary clone of himself. The clone is able to perform all of Gorecrusher's attacks independently of the real one except for his leap, his Wisp Dance and Illusionary summons. If the soul would die it will instead drop down becoming immune and will stop attacking while it regenerates. The soul will resume attacking once it reaches half health and the only way to kill the soul for good is killing Gorecrusher himself.

entities.title: Goreswine the Ravager
entities.description: A mad cultist, too far gone to be really intelligible. The Malevolent being they serve pushes them to desecrate all things, with little regard for practicality. They wear a rotting pig's head as a decorative mask.
entities.location: Roams between the [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=66 Desecrated Cemetery] and the [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=112 Infested Cemetery]

sections.title: Location
sections.body: Goreswine can be found roaming around the southern Farbane Woods, traveling between the [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=66 Desecrated Cemetery] and the [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=112 Infested Cemetery] escorted by four Armoured Skeletons.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
*Corrupted Skull - A ranged attack that fires a single skull and snares the player if it hits.
*Bone Explosion - An explosion that covers the ground in a poison cloud.
*Quad Explosion - They shout "Suffer for us, suffer!", spawns 4 poison clouds total, and teleports elsewhere.
*Ultimate Explosion - At half health they shout "Drink it in, the chaos!", becomes temporarily invulnerable, spawns multiple poison clouds 3 times in a row, and teleports elsewhere.

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty (and Incursion Rifts)
sections.body:
*Corrupted Skull - Their ranged attack now also deals damage over time.
*Bone Explosion - They spawn more Bone explosions per cast.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
Goreswine travels between the two southernmost graveyards in Farbane Woods with an entourage of 4 Armoured Skeletons. While inside the graveyards they will be assisted by numerous skeletons so it's recommended to either clear the skeletons out before fighting them or attack them on the road. Notably they will often run into and attack Lidia the Chaos Archer or Alpha the White Wolf as well as any Creature or Bandits on the road. Even if Goreswine wins this fight, they'll often lose a lot of health making it easier to defeat them.

It is strongly recommended to fight Goreswine in a wide open area so it's less likely that they completely cover the ground in poison. Ranged weapons and spells are also recommended so that the player can continue to attack Goreswine even while they're standing in the middle of his poison.

entities.title: Grayson the Armourer
entities.description: The working arm and logistical mastermind of the bandit forces, Grayson is the backbone of their operation. As the quartermaster of a band of chaotic outlaws, murderers, and thieves, he's the stern voice of reason that keeps their gang well fed and well equipped.

sections.title: Location
sections.body: Grayson can be found in the [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=65 Bandit Armory] in the western Farbane Woods.

sections.title: Dynamic Clouds
sections.body: His arena has dynamic clouds that appear during Daytime.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
*Overhead Swing - Basic melee attack.
*Uppercut - At short range, he runs at the player with an uppercut swing.
*Get Over Here - He throws 3 hammers which pull the player toward him if they get hit.
*Knockback - He shouts "I'm gonna hammer you out!" and does a spin attack that knocks the player back.
*Caltrops - He shouts "I've got the tool for the job!" and throws multiple caltrops to the ground, dealing damage and snaring the player if they step on them. They can be destroyed by equipping the invulnerability armors and walking over them. While invulnerable, the player cannot use any attacks.
*Summon Minion - He shouts "You can't stop me!" and summons a Poacher.

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty
sections.body:
*Get Over Here - Upgraded to throw 5 hammers instead of 3.
*Summon Minion - Upgraded to summon a Deadeye instead of a Poacher.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
Grayson's fight revolves around managing his caltrops by using the 4 armor stands around the arena to turn invulnerable and destroy them. His abilities which knockback and pull the player become much more dangerous while the caltrops are deployed because he can easily push/pull the player into multiple caltrops if they get hit. However, there are only 4 armor stands in his arena so the player needs to be careful not to use them all up too quickly if the fight drags on.

It is advised to prioritize on removing the caltrops in the center of the arena first since they are the ones you're most likely to to be pushed or pulled into. Counter abilities (such as the starting ability ) are very effective at negating his knockbacks if the player can properly time them).

On Brutal Difficulty it is important to prioritize killing his summoned Deadeyes since they're much more threatening than the Poachers.

"Come on legs... work!"

entities.description: A true artist with a deep love for the process of creation. She thinks of herself much like she thinks of her glass. It is beautiful and practical, chaotic and tame, strong and yet delicate. In the same way, her style of glassblowing is methodical and daring. While she is a master of her craft, she wears many savage burn scars for her haphazard approach.

entities.title: Henry Blackbrew the Doctor
entities.description: Doctor Henry Blackbrew was once humankind's last hope against the forces of Dracula, before the Church of Luminance came along. With their newly found faith and weapons of light, mankind turned on the Doctor for his sick methodology and pursuit of human evolution, declaring him a heretic. Banished alongside his students, he went on to found The Trancendum and began constructing a society in his image. With the help of a resource he refers to as "Blood Type E" he's managed to maintain his youth, and keep his twisted pursuit of "progress" alive for well over 800 years.

sections.title: Location
sections.body: Henry can be found in the [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=47 Trancendum Laboratories] in Gloomrot North.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
All attacks inflict Electric Amplify which increases damage taken by 5% per stack.

*Lasers - He'll shoot 4 lasers in every direction.
*Homing Orb - He'll shoot an electrical orb that tracks the player
*Discharge - He'll shout "Try me now!" and do a counter attack.
*Wall Lasers - During the fight, lines of electricity will cross the room and disappear after a while. They can be crossed with a Dash ability.
*Wall Orbs - He'll charge one of the corners of the room and 4 waves of 4 electrical orbs will shoot out.

At half health, he'll surround the area with a ring of electricity and more wall lasers will start to appear.  

*Knockback - He'll charge up a skill at the center of the room and shoot 7 pulses of energy that try to push you against the wall.

sections.title: Quotes
sections.body:
*"Ah, I finally understand, Blood Type E... but too late." (Defeated)
*"I cannot go on, but perhaps you will succeed..." (Defeated)
*"I have failed, and for the final time..." (Defeated)
*"I shall rip the lightning from the sky itself!"

sections.title: Lore
sections.body:
“Dr. Henry Blackbrew was once heralded as a savior of man.

When the hungry fangs of the great conqueror Dracula hung over the throat of man, poised to sink in, the scientific luminary was celebrated. Beloved. The last hope for humankind.

Then came the Light.

Suddenly, Dr. Blackbrew was a heretic, a madman with… ‘twisted, abominable methods.’ Yet, what is petty morality in the pursuit of human perfection? Of evolution? Of knowledge? Even as they came for him, torch and pitchfork in hand, he stood by his philosophies. Even as he was exiled in disgrace to the dangerous and hellish lands of Gloomrot, he KNEW he was correct.

… hundreds of years of a prolonged, unnatural life led to this moment.

This birth of something perfect.

The Monster.”

—From the notes of Callista Alchemica, Senior Electrostatician of the Trancendum [https://blog.stunlock.com/dev-update-19-mood-of-gloomrot/ Gloomrot Dev Blog]

sections.title: Trivia
sections.body:
*Jade the Vampire Hunter is the same Jade from Stunlock Studios' previous title Battlerite. Many of her moves, including her ultimate ability are carried over from the arena brawler title.
*There is speculation that Jade is hunting Nightmarshal Styx the Sunderer to avenge her late brother, who was said to have been killed "by a villain" in her bio in Battlerite. This however, has yet to be confirmed

*Quotes:
**"Bet your head's worth a lot, thanks in advance."
**"You better stick around I don't like cowards."

entities.title: Jakira the Shadow Huntress
entities.description: Jakira was not always a member of the Venom Blades. Like many, she first resisted their onslaught, standing against the great witch Megara and her raiders as they descended upon her homeland and consumed its forests. A master duelist, Jakira always believed in strength, and now she serves the strong with unflinching loyalty. Like many Venom Blades, she's mixed her skills with their corrupted magic, alchemy, and brutal techniques, always looking for new ways to prove herself and earn her place at her masters' side. Despite her stealthy nature, this cocky huntress always warns her prey just before she strikes.

sections.title: Attacks

*Smash - Basic melee attack.
*Crush - It slams the ground, causing a large number of rocks to fall from the ceiling 4 times in a circle radiating out from them. These rocks cannot be blocked by counters.
*Rage - It roars and glows red, automatically snaring the player and gaining increased attack speed for 3 attacks.
*Charge - It crouches on its haunches before charging forward in a straight line.

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty
sections.body:
On brutal difficulty, rocks will continually fall from the ceiling in random locations around the arena.
*Crush - More rocks fall from the ceiling and have a larger area of effect.
*Rage - After roaring, it now also summons a Bear to fight alongside it.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
The key to this fight is dodging the rocks falling from the ceiling while dealing consistent damage to Kodia, so ranged weapons and spells are very useful. 

Kodia's Rage attack is very threatening because it will snare the player no matter where they are in the arena, making it more difficult for them to avoid Kodia's next attacks. It is recommended to save your Veil dash or bring a counter to avoid taking damage until the snare wears off.

entities.title: Kriig the Undead General
entities.description: A truly impressive strategic mind in life, Kriig saw an early end for his mistaken faith in his allies. Though he was sent to an unjust grave, he was like any great mastermind, and had contingencies in place for just such an occasion. A dark deal with an entity of undeath allowed him to rise again and take his revenge. Now he serves the Cult of the Damned with renewed purpose, fully immersing himself into their enigmatic cause.

sections.title: Location
sections.body: Kriig can be found in the [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=74 Haunted Iron Mine] in Dunley Farmlands. Another V Blood, Meredith the Bright Archer, also patrols the same area as Kriig and frequently fights him.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
*Slash - He sweeps his scythe in a wide arc forward, slashing a large area in front of him and on his sides.
*Reaper Whirlwind - His scythe glows green and he draws back his scythe horizontally behind him with both hands, before spinning in a circle while dashing forward. This attack snares the player if it hits them.
*Chain Harpoons - He draws back his left arm and throws 3 harpoons towards the player, which drag them back towards Kriig and briefly snare them if they hit.
*Bone Circle - Kriig raises his scythe in the air, and after a brief delay summons an unholy circle around him that deals damage in melee range.
*Ward of the Damned - He summons a shield similar to the player's , blocking any attacks that hit it and summoning skeletons that fight alongside Kriig.

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty
sections.body:
Every 5 seconds, Kriig will summon an Armoured Skeleton in a random location nearby.
*Reaper Whirlwind - If Kriig hits his skeletons with this ability, they will be afflicted with the Agony effect and glow green. After a few seconds they explode and deal massive damage in an area around them. These explosions can damage other skeletons and even kill them, potentially causing a large chain reaction of explosions.
*Ward of the Damned - He now summons 2 skeletons instead of 1 if the player hits his shield.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
Kriig will frequently fight Meredith the Bright Archer and her Militia entourage, leaving one of them dead and the other on low enough health that they'll be easier to defeat. On brutal difficulty, Kriig will almost always defeat Meredith due to his exploding undead unless the player intervenes to distract him or he spends too long standing on burning ground created by Meredith's Militia Archers. 

If the player chooses not to bait him into fighting Meredith, then he is best fought in his arena at the southernmost end of the mine. This area gives you lots of room to maneuver and is free from dangers present elsewhere in the mine, such as the undead patrols and unholy energy erupting from the ground.

On brutal difficulty, Kriig becomes significantly more threatening especially if he is surrounded by a large number of skeletons that he can explode. Players will greatly benefit from using area of effect spells (such as  and ) to clear them out before he can detonate them. Players must continue to kill his skeletons throughout the fight to prevent them from growing into a massive ticking time bomb.

entities.title: Leandra the Shadow Priestess
entities.description: There are few creatures on the face of Vardoran as ancient as Leandra. Mysterious and surrounded with shadow magic and undeath, it is said that when Dracula fell, and the poisonous blood rains soaked Vardoran, she stood willingly in the deadly downpour. sections.title: Location
sections.body: Leandra can be found in the [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=75 Church of the Damned] in northern Dunley Farmlands.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
*Shadow Bolt - She swings her left arm in a backhand motion, firing a single bolt of shadow at the player
*Shadow Orbs - She holds her left hand behind her as it glows purple, then fires three shadow orbs toward the player. The two orbs on the sides will arc in a semi-circle, and when all 3 orbs converge at the end of their arc they will detonate and deal damage in a large area around them.
*Summon Shadow Soldier - She raises her left hand in the air and summons a shadow soldier that dashes toward the player after a brief delay. The shadow will make a single melee attack and then disappear, but can also be destroyed earlier by taking any amount of damage.

At half health, she'll gain an additional attack:
*Summon Shadow Army - She levitates into the air and shouts "Do you hear them? They're coming!", and disappears as darkness obscures the edges of the player's vision. She then summons 4 shadow soldiers which will attack the player one after the other before disappearing. Leandra can use this ability multiple times per fight.

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty
sections.body:
*Triple Bolt - She swings her left arm in a backhand motion, and fires 3 shadow bolts in parallel lines at the player. She alternates between using this attack and her normal Shadow Bolt attack.
*Shadow Orbs - This ability now summons a shadow soldier after all 3 orbs detonate at the end of their trajectory.
*Summon Shadow Army - This ability now summons 5 shadow soldiers instead of 4.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
This fight revolves around hitting Leandra's shadow soldiers before they hit you first. To that end, weapons with fast basic attacks such as the Sword and Spear will do a better job of eliminating shadows than slower weapons like the Mace or Greatsword. Running two counter abilities (e.g.  and ) can also make this fight a lot easier by giving the player a ton of defensive options for her many shadows and projectiles.

Players should also be on the lookout for Leandra to hold her left hand behind herself as it glows purple since this signals that she's about to fire her Shadow Orbs attack. This is her most threatening attack and will deal massive damage if it catches the player in the detonation at the end of the projectiles' arc.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
Lidia's path through Farbane can cause her to meet and fight with Alpha the White Wolf and/or Goreswine the Ravager. Even if she wins this fight, she'll likely lose a substantial amount of health and thus be easier to defeat. She will also fight any Creature or Undead enemy that crosses her path.

It's essential to fight Lidia in a wide open area with lots of space to maneuver since she will quickly cover the ground in fire and make it difficult to reposition. Row Shots is the ability she'll use most often but it can be avoided by strafing to the left or right and/or by using a barrier spell (e.g.  or ) to block some of the arrows.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
* Double Kill - Styx does two fast slashes and a lunge.
* Death Spin - He spins in a circle firing red blades in a 360° angle dealing damage. His spin attack deals area damage (for  the circle) while the blades deal single target damage.
* Lunge - At 80% health Styx unlocks a new ability. He teleports behind the player and dashes towards them.
* Bat Swarm - He summons three bat-energy balls. Two from the sides closing in on the player and one from the front (it can sometimes curve)
* Gargoyles - At 50% HP he jumps into the air and summons two gargoyles to aid him in the fight.
* Ultimate Power -  Styx levitates into the air darkening the screen of the player and summons 10 of his bat swarm attacks.
* Jump - Styx can now jump into the air and inflict "Heart strike"
* Teleport - He can now teleport behind the player.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
You should be at matched status to Styx or have full set of the upgraded Dread plate armour sanguine weapons and amulet of the blade master.

For spells you should have Ward of the Damned, Veil of Blood,  Blood Fountain and Raging Tempest. You should prioritize healing before attacking. His most problematic attack is his "This is your end" attack or "A few allies".

So you could just tank the hits or heal through them. With ward of the damned counter his double kill attack. For his lunge just sidestep to the sides. Bat friends is the easiest attack to avoid just go forth or backwards. Styx's death spin can be dodged by sidestepping which is the best option just be sure when he does his spin to be far away). For his ultimate attack you should just heal through it plus Styx takes reduced damage during this move.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
During the fight, Lucile will periodically spawn a variety of throwable potions, which she will occassionally attempt to drink throughout the fight. Along the walls in her lab are respawning shelves filled with them. Destroying a shelf will drop a random one on the floor:
*  - Polymorphs all targets in the area into Sheep. Is required to end Lucile's "Alchemic Madness" state.
*  - Sets the area and all targets entering it on fire. The burn makes Gold Golems vulnerable to attacks for the duration. Instantly kills Corrupted Mantrap.
*  - Dramatically increases player movement speed and maximizes crit chance.
*  - Knocks targets back and dispels all effects on targets hit, including Lucile's "Gold Skin" invulnerability.
*  - Applies a healing buff to targets in the area. Taking damage ends the effect.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
*Paper Barrage - She swings her book in front of her, firing 4 lines of pages at the player.
*Ink Bolt - She holds her left hand back then swings her wand and fires an ink projectile at the player. If it hits them, it summons an Ink Demon to aid Maja. This projectile pierces through enemies and can therefore summon multiple Ink Demons in a single cast if it hits multiple players or summons (e.g. the skeletons created by Unholy spells).
*Ink Splatter - She shouts "Flee interloper!" or "A taste of knowledge!", then creates a large ink area around her that explodes after a brief delay and summons an Ink Demon.
*Summon Ink Demons - She creates a small burst of ink dealing damage in an area around her, shouts "Rise Demons! Accept these vessels!" or "Witness my little devils!", then disappears while 3 ink projectiles begin springing up out of the ground. These projectiles create Ink Demons upon landing and will also snare the player if they hit them. Maja reappears in a random location once this attack ends.
*Consume - She shouts "A sacrifice is required!" or "Lend me your power!" before channeling to create a large book in front of her that shields an Ink Demon and begins to drag it towards her. If the Ink Demon is dragged all the way to the book, it slams shut around it, destroying the demon and healing Maja for a substantial amount of health. This ability can be canceled by killing the demon before it reaches the book.

At half health, she'll gain an additional attack:
*Paper Cut - She shouts "Death by a thousand paper cuts!" or "The exquisite suffering of a paper cut!" or "Here is some mandatory reading!" or "Do you also thirst for research?!", and summons 7 lines of pages that fire at the player, followed by 7 more from a different angle after a delay. These projectiles are spaced further apart than those created by her Paper Barrage ability and can be avoided by standing between them.

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty
sections.body:
On brutal difficulty, 3 Flying Books passively fly in circles around the arena and deal damage to the player if they hit them.
*Paper Cut - She is now able to use this ability even before dropping below half health.
*Consume - If she successfully consumes an Ink Demon, she now creates 3 ink blobs that fall in an area around her, summoning 3 new Ink Demons where they land.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body: This fight is filled to the brim with projectiles, making counter and barrier spells (e.g.  or ) extremely valuable to avoid taking damage. It is particularly important to avoid getting hit with Ink Bolt since this will summon more Ink Demons to assist Maja. Spells which summon minions (e.g. , ) are strongly disincentivized in this fight since they will easily get hit by Maja's Ink Bolt, allowing her to summon additional Ink Demons.

"Out! Out! OUT!!!"

"No one will hinder my research!"
