This projectile pierces through enemies and can therefore summon multiple Ink Demons in a single cast if it hits multiple players or summons (e.g. the skeletons created by Unholy spells).
Ink Splatter - She shouts "Flee interloper!" or "A taste of knowledge!", then creates a large ink area around her that explodes after a brief delay and summons an Ink Demon.
Summon Ink Demons - She creates a small burst of ink dealing damage in an area around her, shouts "Rise Demons! Accept these vessels!" or "Witness my little devils!", then disappears while 3 ink projectiles begin springing up out of the ground. These projectiles create Ink Demons upon landing and will also snare the player if they hit them. Maja reappears in a random location once this attack ends.
Consume - She shouts "A sacrifice is required!" or "Lend me your power!" before channeling to create a large book in front of her that shields an Ink Demon and begins to drag it towards her. If the Ink Demon is dragged all the way to the book, it slams shut around it, destroying the demon and healing Maja for a substantial amount of health. entities.title: Megara the Serpent Queen
entities.description:
There was once a small village of warriors, a place of little significance. When the great witch Megara appeared the villagers reacted with suspicion, gathering their forces to stand against her. Megara gave them a display of power that inspired such terror it crushed all hope of resistance, driving them to their knees.

"I am your Queen! The greatest half of you will become my first subjects, and will walk by my side. Come dusk, each of you that are holding the heart of one of your neighbors will earn your place."

Those who obeyed became the first Venom Blades, worthy of receiving the secret of Venom Sap. This fuels their war effort, but more importantly, the great witch herself.

sections.title: Location
sections.body: Megara can be found in the [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=105 Venom Blades Bastion] in Oakveil Woodlands.

sections.title: Dynamic Clouds
sections.body: Her arena has dynamic clouds that appear during Daytime.

sections.title: Phase 1
sections.body:
Megara is found at the center of the arena, surrounded by her followers. damaging them or Megara herself causes her to initiate combat, instantly killing her followers and pushing back the player. 

* Activate wells: Causes two wells to activate and throw area targeted balls of venom around which make puddles on the ground for a while. Deals moderate damage.
* Venom bolt: Throws an area targeted bolt of venom, jumping around twice before disappearing.
* Spiralling venom: Causes an explosion in an area dealing moderate damage. Multiple venom bolts will spiral out of the location, which deal minor damage and can be blocked.
* Scream: Dashes towards (or away from, if too close) the target and winds up a scream in a cone which knocks back and deals serious damage.
* Laser: Winds up a linear laser and tries to intercept the target before shooting it, dealing serious damage. 
* Volley: Dashes around, then launches a volley of four homing projectiles (two on each side). Can be blocked, each projectile deals moderate damage.
* Flight: Levitates and becomes untargetable, moves to the other side of the arena while shooting area targeted projectiles dealing moderate damage.

sections.title: Phase 2
sections.body:
Megara levitates and moves to the venom pool at the northern center, transforming to her true form. For the rest of the fight:

* Megara will have a body and a tail, both being targetable and active.
* Neither the body nor the tail can move around, being only able to move between wells (while they start at the northern pool, neither parts will go back there) . Once the body submerges, the runes around the well she'll emerge from will glow white.
* The tail only has a slam ability which stuns, with hits being practically lethal as it leave you defenceless to the body's abilities.
* The body will use different abilities based on distance to the target.
* A venom storm will appear around the arena, closing in at times forcing you to get close to the boss.

sections.title: Close distance
sections.body:
* Swing: Swings her blade in an arc. Can be blocked, deals serious damage.
* Cleave: Slams down her blade, then cleaves in an arc which also releases projectiles in the same arc. Can be blocked, deals serious damage.
* Skewer: Skewers the target, dealing serious damage and incapacitating. 
* Venom rain: Shoots multiple area targeted venom bolts around herself, dealing moderate damage.

sections.title: Close and medium distance
sections.body:
* Spiralling venom: Similar to the first phase.
* Scream: Winds up a giant cone, then screams dealing serious damage and knocking back the targets.
* Laser: Similar to the first phase, but shoots twice.

sections.title: Long distance
sections.body: * Venom barrage: Summons multiple orbs at the sides (and potentially behind herself), each shooting projectiles in lines, The venom storm will close in, forcing players to move to her location. Each projectile deals minor damage. Can be blocked.

sections.title: Phase 3
sections.body: Megara will use the same abilities at the second phase. She also periodically summons four spiralling disks, which can be blocked and deal moderate damage.

sections.title: Lore
sections.body:
Secret rituals, heart-wrenching venom, and black magic. The Serpent Queen Megara emerged from the mist, driven by dark mysteries on a relentless mission of destruction. Surrounded by her loathsome raiders, the Venom Blades, every shore she touches withers with corruption.

All hail the Serpent Queen! All fear the Serpent Queen! All must be consumed… by the Serpent Queen."

entities.title: Meredith the Bright Archer
entities.description: Meredith is a true believer in the Church of Luminance. She believes her power is a gift from the Light to wield against dark forces, much as the original Paladins were given the Light to strike down Dracula and the Vampire legions. As brave as she is naive to the Church’s descent into avarice and gluttony, this holy archer is blinded by the light, focused only on her pursuit of justice at any cost.

sections.title: Location
sections.body: Meredith can be found patrolling the [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=88 Haunted Iron Mine] in southern Dunley Farmlands. She is escorted by 2 Militia Archers and 2 Militia Guards. She will patrol the mine while attacking any undead she comes across, including Kriig the Undead General, but will occasionally exit the mine and take a brief break before returning to her hunt.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
Her arrows will heal her Militia allies if they strike them.
*Arrow Shot - She fires a single arrow at the player.
*Blessed Shot - She shouts "Bless this shot!" then fires an an arrow in the direction the player is moving, predicting their path. This arrow deals heavy damage and incapacitates the player if it hits them.
*Dash - She occasionally dashes around the area up to 4 times, damaging targets she passes through.

At half health, she'll gain 2 additional attacks:
*Summon Militia Guard - She shouts "For Luminance!", and summons 2 Militia Guards.
*Arrow Barrage - She shouts "Light, guide my arrows!", then shoots 10 arrows upward that will fall around her. This attack stuns the player if they get hit.

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty
sections.body:
*Arrow Shot - This ability now fires 6 arrows in a cone in front of her instead of just 1.
*Blessed Shot - This ability can now ricochet off of other enemies or the terrain.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
Meredith will frequently fight Kriig the Undead General and his skeleton warriors, leaving one of them dead and the other on low enough health that they'll be easier to defeat. On brutal difficulty, Kriig will almost always defeat Meredith due to his exploding undead unless the player intervenes to distract him or he spends too long standing on burning ground created by Meredith's militia archers. 

If the player chooses not to bait her into fighting Kriig, then it is still highly recommended to fight her inside the mine rather than at its entrance. Any militia soldiers and passing V Bloods (such as Vincent the Frostbringer, Christina the Sun Priestess, and Simon Belmont the Vampire Hunter) will come to Meredith's aid if they spot her fighting there. 

Meredith is most easily fought with ranged weapons and spells that allow the player to damage her while dodging her arrows and stuns. Her Blessed Shot can be avoided by moving back and forth to confuse her predictive tracking. It is also recommended to be wary of her summoned Militia Guards, since their shield barrier can stun the player if they attack into it.

"The Luminance has guided you to me! I must do this!"

"My arrows will strike true. My faith is unshakeable!"

"I'm too tired... I can't keep fighting..."

"...Save me..."

"Why is it so...dark?"

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
*Bite - The standard melee attack.
*Rage - Nibbles glows red, then melee attacks 6 times in a row.
*Poison Explosion - Nibbles shakes its coat and releases a green poison mist that explodes in an area around it after a delay.
*Summon Minions - Nibbles burrows into the ground, temporarily leaving the fight while summoning 3 s. More rats will steadily join the fight until 9 have been summoned in total.

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty
sections.body: *Poison Explosion - The explosion will now be released instantly when Nibbles uses Rage and then again after a delay.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
Due to how it is summoned, Nibbles can be easily fought when and where the player desires. Placing the Vermin Nest in front of a road patrolled by powerful V Bloods (such as Tristan the Vampire Hunter or Simon Belmont the Vampire Hunter) can lead to them killing it for you. Nibbles will also fight strong regular enemies such as Stone Golems and Treants, so the player can summon him in a land plot where these enemies are lying in wait. Alternatively, the player can wait till they've acquired and outfitted several strong Servants before fighting Nibbles alongside them.

The player should be careful not to accidentally lock themself into or out of their home by summoning Nibbles near the entrance when they aren't yet strong enough to defeat it. If this occurs then they may need to lure higher level enemies to fight Nibbles for them or to set up a temporary second base where they can upgrade their gear to a high enough level.

Nibbles' Poison Explosion attack is by far its most dangerous attack, especially on Brutal difficulty where it is hard to predict. As a result, it is recommended to use ranged weapons and spells to avoid fighting it in melee range and to summon it in a large area where the player can move about freely. Area of effect spells (such as  or ) are also recommended to deal with the rat minions.

A ranged weapon will also help the player attack him while maintaining distance to better dodge his skull projectiles.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
All her attacks as well as her spirit's attacks can pass through all targets in their path. If hitting the player, they deal damage. If hitting Polora or her spirits, then they heal them.
*Spirit Wave - Polora does a stationary channel, lifting her left arm up, before releasing 3 spread out spirit projectiles that move in a wave-like pattern.
*Spirit Wolf - Polora does a short channel in front of her before launching a spirit wolf in a straight line. The wolf deals damage/heals depending on target hit. After a short delay, the wolf will bounce to a new target, up to 5 times, for a total of 6 hits. It can bounce back to Polora.
*Fear - If the player is in close proximity to Polora, she'll shout "Begone!"and start a second long channel. When it ends she will Fear all targets in a small radius around her, forcing them to run away from her.
*Invisibility - If the player is in close proximity to Polora, she will turn invisible for a few seconds, and gain increased movement speed. If afflicted by , her movement can be tracked.
*Summon Minion - After losing 25% of her health, Polora will periodically shout "Spirits, hear me!" and summon a Pixie. They fire ranged wave-like spirit attacks, but their aiming turn rate is slower. If killed, Polora may resummon a new one.

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty
sections.body:
On brutal difficulty, her healing is significantly increased
*Spirit Wave - She now fires projectiles in a full 360-degree wave all around her instead of just 3 in front of her.
*Summon Minion - She now summons 2 pixies instead of 1.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
When fighting Polora, positioning is key. Allowing her to hit you with her projectiles will quickly heal her, and allowing her projectiles to hit her pixies will heal them. In the worst case, she and her pixies can fire projectiles that heal each other while damaging you. Note that this makes spells from the Unholy spell tree less desirable in this fight since she and her pixies can heal off of damage dealt to the skeletons. 

The best way to deal with these projectiles is to block them with barrier spells (e.g. ) while also using area of effect spells to deal consistent damage to both Polora and her pixies. A ranged weapon can also help since her she won't use Fear unless the player is too close to her.

combat.fightGuide:
All her attacks as well as her spirit's attacks can pass through all targets in their path. If hitting the player, they deal damage. If hitting Polora or her spirits, then they heal them.
Spirit Wave - Polora does a stationary channel, lifting her left arm up, before releasing 3 spread out spirit projectiles that move in a wave-like pattern.
Spirit Wolf - Polora does a short channel in front of her before launching a spirit wolf in a straight line. The wolf deals damage/heals depending on target hit. After a short delay, the wolf will bounce to a new target, up to 5 times, for a total of 6 hits. It can bounce back to Polora.
Fear - If the player is in close proximity to Polora, she'll shout "Begone!"and start a second long channel. When it ends she will Fear all targets in a small radius around her, forcing them to run away from her.
Invisibility - If the player is in close proximity to Polora, she will turn invisible for a few seconds, and gain increased movement speed. If afflicted by , her movement can be tracked.
Summon Minion - After losing 25% of her health, Polora will periodically shout "Spirits, hear me!" and summon a Pixie. They fire ranged wave-like spirit attacks, but their aiming turn rate is slower. If killed, Polora may resummon a new one.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
*Double Swipe - His basic melee attack consists of 2 swipes with his mace.
*Shock Wave - After a brief charge, he'll do a knockback melee attack that inflicts a minor  debuff. He'll then create 4 waving shockwave lines that explode after a couple seconds that also inflict the lesser . Stacks with regular .
*Mace Throw - He throws his weapon, tracking player movement and snaring them if it hits.
*Chaos Barrier - He shouts "Show me what you've got!" and creates a reflective shield that inflicts  if hit. The shield does not deflect AoE attacks such as  or the crossbow's Rain of Bolts.
*Summon Minion - He shouts "Rise to the challenge!" and spawns a Trapper.
*Merciless Charge - His shield will shine for a second before he does a charge attack that does heavy damage and stuns.
*Triple Charge - At half health he shouts "A rousing battle!" and does 3 charges in a row. He'll be briefly stunned afterwards.

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty
sections.body:
*Summon Minion - He now spawns a Stalker instead of a Trapper. The Stalker has a ranged spear attack that drags the player toward her.
*Merciless Charge - His charge now leaves behind a trail of flames that apply .
*Triple Charge - His triple charge now leaves behind a trail of flames that apply . He can also now use this ability multiple times in the fight.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
This fight greatly rewards the player for paying attention to Quincey's audio and visual cues, which indicate which attack he's about to use before he does it. This can enable the player to predict and side step many of his attacks, allowing them to save their defensive abilities for emergencies.

Quincey's Mace Throw is deceptively strong and can frequently catch players off guard because it has no audio cue to forewarn them and a very fast animation. It is recommended to save your Veil dash or use a counter/barrier ability to avoid this attack since the snare can prevent you from avoiding any follow-up attacks. 

It is important to kill Quincey's minions quickly since the Trapper's net throw and the Stalker's harpoon attack can root or reposition the player so that they end up taking massive damage from Quincey's Shock Wave.

Killing Nicholaus the Fallen before fighting Quincey can be beneficial since it gives early game players their first ultimate ability (either  or ) for this fight. It is recommended to use the latter over the former since it deals high damage and the Army of the Dead dies very quickly to Quincey's Shock Wave attack.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
*Crossbow Bolt - Rufus' standard attack. He fires a crossbow bolt with a red glow in a straight line.
*Throw Net - Much like the Trapper ability, Rufus swings a net around before throwing it into the AoE indicator. Any player still in that zone when he throws the net will be pinned in place for several seconds.
*Dodge Roll - If the player draws too close to him he can dodge-roll away.
*Summon Minions - Rufus calls for some minions, a Thug and a Poacher, to join the fight. 
*Rage - Rufus will shield himself and any of his nearby allies, similar to the Blood Rage ability.
*Rapid Crossbow - Once Rufus gets to about half health he says "I'm gonna call you target practice!" and fires 8 crossbow bolts in rapid succession. After that the weapon will clinck, indicating to the player that the attack is over.

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty (and Incursion Rifts)
sections.body: *Much of his fight is unchanged except he reacts faster, and can use his Rapid Crossbow attack sooner than the 50% HP interval.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
Attacking during the day may be dangerous as there isn't always a great deal of shade to hide in, and so getting hit by a net in the sun can prove fatal. It is also advisable to clear the area of any Bandits before engaging him.

Rufus's most dangerous move is his Rapid Crossbow attack, which can easily kill a player within seconds if they are unprepared for it. It is important to save your Veil dash for this attack so that he wastes most of his shots.

sections.title: Location
sections.body: Sir Erwin can be found at the [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=107 Horse Racing Track] in the west of Dunley Farmlands.

sections.title: Dynamic Clouds
sections.body: His arena has dynamic clouds that appear during Daytime.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
Erwin fights on horseback, granting him significant movement speed.
*Swipe - His basic melee attack consisting of a delayed horizontal swing with his sword. This attack has low range but swings in a wide arc.
*Twin Lightning - He shouts "Twin Lightning!" or "Spears of Glory!" and fires 2 Ball Lightning projectiles. These projectiles track where the player is moving and launch in that direction rather than directly at the player. He will sometimes cancel this ability early to use another one, resulting in only 1 or even 0 projectiles.
*Holy Artillery - He shouts "Holy Artillery!" or "From the Heavens!" and 2 area of effect lightning blasts strike from the sky after a brief delay.
*Stunning Leap - His horse leaps high into the air, then crashes down dealing lightning damage in a large area. Erwin is briefly stunned after landing.
*Lightning Charge - He shouts "Bravely forward, Charger!", "Sally forth!", or "Charge!!!" and charges at the player, stunning them if he hits.
*Hyper Charge - His horse rears up on its hind legs, he raises his sword in the air, shouts "Charger, I think I've got it!", "Charge like thunder!", or "The Heavens are on my side!" and charges toward the player while small lightning bolts strike in a wave that follows his charge.

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty
sections.body: *Lightning Charge - While using this attack he now summons a lightning horse that charges alongside him and stuns the player if it hits. The lightning horse remains after he uses this move and continues to charge and attempt to stun the player even while Erwin uses other attacks. Erwin can have multiple lightning horses on the field if he uses this move again before the first horse has been dealt with, however each horse has a very low amount of health.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
Erwin's high movement speed on horseback can make him challenging to keep up with, so ranged abilities such as  and Iron tier and above Axes'  are particularly effective here.

Twin Lightning is one of Erwin's most frequent attacks but can be easily dodged if you learn how to bait it. This attack will always attempt to fire in the direction that the player is moving, so abruptly changing direction as he fires it will often lead to it missing.

On brutal difficulty, it is absolutely essential to kill his lightning horse summons as soon as possible. They have very little health so they should die quickly but are very fast and can make the fight extremely difficult by stunning the player or forcing them to split their attention between Erwin and the horse.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body: Solarus the Immaculate has three phases. It is recommended for multiple players to attempt this fight together, but can still be accomplished solo, albeit with more difficulty.

sections.title: Phase 1
sections.body:
*Buzzsaw - Solarus will perform a slow, wide swing in front of himself before chopping down while firing a buzzsaw projectile. After travelling for a while, the buzzsaw will split in two, one going to the left and one to the right, before returning towards Solarus, converging in front of him.
*Light Wave - Solarus will spawn a large amount of projectiles on either side of him that, forming two semicircles as they spread out, with a small amount of space between each projectile.
*Charge - Solarus will prepare to charge, aiming ahead of where the player is moving in an attempt to intercept them. In the wake of his charge, projectiles will be fired on either side of him in a tight formation. If Solarus hits the player he will deal damage and stun the player.
*Luminance - Starting at around 70% health, Solarus will go into the middle of the arena, shout "This is luminance", and spawn two light vortexes, one to his left and one to his right. The vortexes each shoot 3 projectiles in a spiraling pattern. The vortexes fire at slightly different angles.
*Divine Angel - At 50% health, Solarus will summon a Divine Angel to assist him in battle. While the angel can be damaged during this phase it cannot be killed, becoming immune and beginning to regenerate if brought down to half health. During this time, the angel doesn't attack. As the angel is the focus of phase 2, it's attacks will be discussed there. The player will take damage in a small area around where the angel is summoned.

sections.title: Phase 2
sections.body:
This phase starts when Solarus is close to death during the first phase. Solarus will become immune to all damage and begin summoning beams of light that sweep across the arena, damaging everything they touch. On Brutal Solarus will also regen his health. This phase ends when the angel summoned in the first phase is killed. The angel's attacks are as follows:

*Swipe Combo - The angel will quickly swipe twice in front of themselves before thrusting their spear forwards. The thrust shoots out several more thrusts forwards. If the player is too close to the angel, the thrusts will bypass block, damaging the player.

*Charge - The angel will quickly charge forwards, dealing damage and knocking aside the player if the charge connects.

*Bolts - The angel will begin shooting bolts of light that explode, dealing damage and knocking aside the player if they are caught in the area. The bolts will damage and knock the player aside even through block.

*Empowered Light Wave - This attack is similar to Solarus' light wave, although the angel will fire more projectiles in an hourglass shape after the initial semicircle.

sections.title: Phase 3
sections.body:
After defeating the angel it will slowly be corrupted into a Fallen Angel. Once this is done, they will break Solarus' immunity and continue aiding the player during this phase until it dies. Solarus' gains new attacks in this phase while only losing his melee attack from last phase, it being replaced with a stronger version.

*Buzzsaw Combo - Solarus will quickly slash in front of himself three times before slashing downwards, firing two buzzsaws in a V pattern in front of himself. As expected, each buzzsaw will split into two then return to Solarus.

*Light Beams - Solarus will summon beams of light to sweep across the arena, which are identical to the ones from phase 2. The beams will linger for a while, becoming a threat during Solarus' other attacks.

*Leap - Solarus will leap at the player, dealing damage in a wide array around himself as he lands. If the player is hit by the leap they will become incapacitated. Solarus will always follow up the leap with heavy swing that does high damage and throws the player backwards. The leap cannot be countered or blocked.

sections.title: Other Notes
sections.body:
#Solarus is not immune while casting Luminance.
#Solarus will prioritize charging at the player over using his Light Wave attack.
#Phase 2 can begin in the middle of Solarus' attacks, although it won't interrupt said attacks.
#Both Phase 3 Solarus and The Angel drop healing orbs at half health (this is not the case on Brutal).
#The angel can fly over the pit around the arena which makes it likely to start firing bolts at the player while staying completely outside of melee reach.
#While the Fallen Angel does help the player in phase 3, it is still considered an enemy meaning it can accidentally block the player's attacks. This, however, can be used by the player to heal themselves if they have any life leeching effects.
#While the Fallen Angel does attack Solarus, it doesn't seem to do any damage. This does mean however that the player doesn't need to worry about the angel hitting them on accident.

sections.title: Equipment and Abilities
sections.body: It is highly advised for the player to use the full Bloodmoon Armour set, a sanguine or ancestral weapon of their choosing and an upgrade of the Blood Merlot Amulet. For weapons, a reaper with it's Howling Reaper ability can do a lot of damage to Solarus as he frequently stands still during both his buzzsaw attacks as well as his Luminance attack. For abilities, counters and blocks are always good defensive options. Abilities that are hard to hit usually, such as  or , are worth considering as they are easier to hit for the same reason Howling Reaper is easy to hit. Lastly,  can usually deal its full damage to Solarus as the majority of the fight he will be isolated, though the player should wait until The Fallen Angel in phase 3 dies to use this again.

sections.title: The Fight
sections.body: General tips: The fight with Solarus can be seen as a mix of the fights with Gorecrusher the Behemoth and The Winged Horror, which prior to the Gloomrot update preceded him. Like with Gorecrusher, Solarus' attacks reward the player for making more aggressive choices, such as using their Travel Ability to go towards the boss rather than away from them, this being discussed later. Furthermore, Solarus covers a lot of area both with his projectile attacks and his phase 2 and phase 3 beams of light, similarly to The Winged Horror. Lastly, during phase 3, the Fallen Angel should be hit as little as possible unless the player desperately needs healing and their only way of getting any is through life leeching effects. The best course of action is to let Solarus kill the angel while you attack him from afar. That said, Solarus will still sometimes attack the player rather than the angel so it is advised to remain cautious.

General tips: The fight with Solarus can be seen as a mix of the fights with Gorecrusher the Behemoth and The Winged Horror, which prior to the Gloomrot update preceded him. Like with Gorecrusher, Solarus' attacks reward the player for making more aggressive choices, such as using their Travel Ability to go towards the boss rather than away from them, this being discussed later. Furthermore, Solarus covers a lot of area both with his projectile attacks and his phase 2 and phase 3 beams of light, similarly to The Winged Horror. Lastly, during phase 3, the Fallen Angel should be hit as little as possible unless the player desperately needs healing and their only way of getting any is through life leeching effects. The best course of action is to let Solarus kill the angel while you attack him from afar. That said, Solarus will still sometimes attack the player rather than the angel so it is advised to remain cautious.

phases.title: Phase 1
phases.body:
Buzzsaw - Solarus will perform a slow, wide swing in front of himself before chopping down while firing a buzzsaw projectile. After travelling for a while, the buzzsaw will split in two, one going to the left and one to the right, before returning towards Solarus, converging in front of him.
Light Wave - Solarus will spawn a large amount of projectiles on either side of him that, forming two semicircles as they spread out, with a small amount of space between each projectile.
Charge - Solarus will prepare to charge, aiming ahead of where the player is moving in an attempt to intercept them. In the wake of his charge, projectiles will be fired on either side of him in a tight formation. If Solarus hits the player he will deal damage and stun the player.
Luminance - Starting at around 70% health, Solarus will go into the middle of the arena, shout "This is luminance", and spawn two light vortexes, one to his left and one to his right. The vortexes each shoot 3 projectiles in a spiraling pattern. The vortexes fire at slightly different angles.
Divine Angel - At 50% health, Solarus will summon a Divine Angel to assist him in battle. While the angel can be damaged during this phase it cannot be killed, becoming immune and beginning to regenerate if brought down to half health. During this time, the angel doesn't attack. As the angel is the focus of phase 2, it's attacks will be discussed there. The player will take damage in a small area around where the angel is summoned.

phases.title: Phase 2
phases.body:
This phase starts when Solarus is close to death during the first phase. Solarus will become immune to all damage and begin summoning beams of light that sweep across the arena, damaging everything they touch. On Brutal Solarus will also regen his health. This phase ends when the angel summoned in the first phase is killed. The angel's attacks are as follows:
Swipe Combo - The angel will quickly swipe twice in front of themselves before thrusting their spear forwards. The thrust shoots out several more thrusts forwards. If the player is too close to the angel, the thrusts will bypass block, damaging the player.
Charge - The angel will quickly charge forwards, dealing damage and knocking aside the player if the charge connects.
Bolts - The angel will begin shooting bolts of light that explode, dealing damage and knocking aside the player if they are caught in the area. The bolts will damage and knock the player aside even through block.
Empowered Light Wave - This attack is similar to Solarus' light wave, although the angel will fire more projectiles in an hourglass shape after the initial semicircle.

phases.title: Phase 3
phases.body:
After defeating the angel it will slowly be corrupted into a Fallen Angel. Once this is done, they will break Solarus' immunity and continue aiding the player during this phase until it dies. Solarus' gains new attacks in this phase while only losing his melee attack from last phase, it being replaced with a stronger version.
Buzzsaw Combo - Solarus will quickly slash in front of himself three times before slashing downwards, firing two buzzsaws in a V pattern in front of himself. As expected, each buzzsaw will split into two then return to Solarus.
Light Beams - Solarus will summon beams of light to sweep across the arena, which are identical to the ones from phase 2. The beams will linger for a while, becoming a threat during Solarus' other attacks.
Leap - Solarus will leap at the player, dealing damage in a wide array around himself as he lands. If the player is hit by the leap they will become incapacitated. Solarus will always follow up the leap with heavy swing that does high damage and throws the player backwards. The leap cannot be countered or blocked.

phases.title: Phase 1
phases.body:
Buzzsaw: The player can safely walk out of the swing range of Solarus before sidestepping the buzzsaw. Afterwards, if the player walks unto the very tip of Solarus' sword, or slightly above, then they should be safe from the boomeranging buzzsaws. The player can also choose to get behind Solarus with their Travel Ability, as the buzzsaws do not cover any ground directly behind him. However, when using  this might become riskier as Solarus can turn fairly quickly after the swing and the Veil in question is, strangely, the only one that doesn't hide the player after the initial dash.
Light Wave: Using your Travel Ability to pass through the point where the two semicircles overlap is the safest way of dodging this attack. Alternatively, the player can use their Travel Ability to get right next to Solarus during this attack as it does not hit directly in front of him apart from the very start. This, however, is very risky. Alternatively the player can use a barrier of their choice, damaging Solarus or healing themselves in the process.
Charge: The first way to safely dodge this attack is moving either left or right while Solarus is preparing the attack. Then, when Solarus is about to charge, start moving in the opposite direction of where you were initially going while staying in front of the boss so as to not get hit by the bolts that come after the dash. The second way of dodging this attack is getting behind Solarus while he charges with your Travel Ability or to simply counter or block the charge.
Luminance: Staying as far away from the vortexes during this attack will give the player as much time to react to each bolt as possible. The player should also use this time to damage Solarus with ranged attacks. A good place to stay is the entrance to the arena.

phases.title: Phase 3
phases.body:
Unmentioned Attacks: These attacks have already been covered previously and are dodged in the same way as previously mentioned. The only attack that this doesn't apply to is the Buzzsaw attack as that one doesn't make an appearance during this phase.
Buzzsaw Combo: The initial swing comes out fast, combined with the fact that the following two swings leave no pause in between make countering, blocking or dashing away from Solarus the only reliable way of avoiding damage. As for the two buzzsaws, simply walking away from Solarus without going left or right will dodge the initial two buzzsaws and standing a a short distance away from Solarus' sword should also dodge the four boomeranging buzzsaws. The player can also dodge the buzzsaws if they are right next to them before splitting. Dashing behind Solarus still works, although the player should wait before revealing themselves so as to not let Solarus turn around.
Leap: The leap can be avoided with the Travel Ability. However, Solarus will always follow up with his wide swing which can do upwards of 100 damage meaning the player should avoid it at all costs. As such, after dodging the leap, the player should make as much distance between themselves and Solarus as possible, or to go behind him. If the leap connects with the player, there is no way of dodging the swing as the incapacitate effect will keep the player still for just long enough to get hit.

entities.title: Stavros the Carver
entities.description: One will not expect a simple craftsman to be so vicious in battle, but none represent the Venom Blades' endless thirst for havoc and consumption better that Stavros. From carving the trees with runes of corruption to harvesting the Venom Sap those trees produce, he works with a cold glee. Whether it be bark or flesh, every cut of his knife is a show of his devotion to the great witch Megara. Like any Venom Blade, he loves and fears his queen in equal measure, revering her as a goddess and looking to her for higher purpose.

sections.title: Lore
sections.body: "Once the ritual is complete and the trees are fully corrupted, swollen with Venom Sap, they are felled, collected, and drained dry. This grisly process is overseen by Stavros the Carver, a fanatical servant of the Serpent Queen and an unquestionably murderous psychopath. Few among the Venom Blades dare to consume Venom Sap directly, let alone wield it in its raw, volatile form. Stavros is no ordinary zealot, though bold may not be the correct word for what he is."

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
At first, due to the large amount of projectiles The Winged Horror has, all the burning ground some of these projectiles leave behind as well as it's very strong melee attacks, the fight can seem exceedingly hard. However, this fight rewards patience rather than aggression and, once the player realizes this, makes the fight the easiest one out of the endgame bosses.

*Retreat - During the fight, The Winged Horror will retreat directly away from the player whenever they get close. This weirdly happens even if The Winged Horror itself gets close to the player instead of the other way around.
*Debuffs - The Winged Horror fight features two unique debuffs. The first is a damage over time, applied by it's Chaos attacks and the second one slowing down the player, applied by it's Frost attacks. If the player is burning and gets hit with a frost attack the burning will be cleansed and the slowing effect will take effect, and vice versa. This makes it so the player can never be affected by both debuffs at the same time. The debuffs last for about 10 seconds each.
*Projectiles - The Winged Horror's projectiles are either Chaos Volley style fireballs or Crystal Lance icicles, applying the burning and slowing debuffs respectively. The icicles in particular always split into two additional icicles, forming a Y pattern. These secondary icicles do not split further.
*Fire Breath - The Winged Horror flies up and spews fire down to the ground in one spot for a few seconds. Fireballs will shoot out from the location of the stream. When the fireballs land they deal damage and scorch the ground. The player will take damage and be inflicted with the burning debuff if they step on the scorched ground.
*Flare Charge - The Winged Horror will unfurl it's wings one at a time while also summoning a fireball on either side of it's body. Afterwards, it and the fireballs quickly charge towards the location it was facing, dealing damage to the player. If the player is hit by The Winged Horror instead of the fireballs, they will be pushed back and will very likely be attacked by a swipe. If the player is behind The Winged Horror, it is likely The Horror will attempt a Tail Whip instead. Later in the fight, the charge will spread scorched ground if it comes into contact with any.
*Swipe and Tail whip - The Winged Horror swipes forwards with it claws or whips with it's tail. Both attacks deal damage in an arc while shooting a volley of icicles. The tail whip is used only when the player is behind The Winged Horror.
*Spin - The Winged Horror curls up before spinning in place, dealing damage around itself and knocking back players while firing icicles all around itself.
*Fireball Drop - Starting at around 70% health, The Winged Horrror will fly up and across the battlefield while dropping fireballs that scorch the earth. Once it's done dropping fireballs, The Horror will violently crash back down to the arena. As the fight progresses, The Horror will do multiple flights over the battlefield, each with it's own set of fireballs.
*Frost Vortex - Starting at around 70% health, The Winged Horror will roar, causing snow to build up in an area. Shortly afterwards, a blizzard will appear in the area, dealing damage to players inside.
*Fireball Volley 1 - Starting at around 50% health, The Winged Horror will breathe 4 sets of fireballs in a semi-circle in front of itself. The first and third set of fireballs are lighter in color and have consistent speed while the second and fourth set have darker and move at different speeds, causing them to cover the space between the first and third set's space in between the fireballs. The fireballs leave behind scorched earth when they disappear.
*Fireball Volley 2 - Starting at around 30% health, The Winged Horror will spawn 2 Chaos vortexes on either side of itself and begin violently batting it's wings, causing a strong gust of wind. The player is pushed back constantly by the wind while the vortexes shoot fireballs towards the

sections.title: Other notes
sections.body:
#There seems to be a limit as to how much scorched earth can be present at any given time.
#When icicles split they explode in a small radius. This explosion deals no damage to the player but does debuff them with the slowing debuff, making it a way of cleansing the damage overtime debuff.
#Due to the arena being on a mountain peak with very little shade, the fight will likely be abandoned if it becomes daytime unless The Winged Horror is nearly defeated.
#While in the air, The Winged Horror cannot be hit.

sections.title: Equipment and Abilities
sections.body:
Due to this being an endgame boss, be prepared with a Bloodmoon Armour set, Amulets magic source and Sanguine tier weapons. More specifically, the best weapons for this fight are ranged weapons such as pistols or crossbows or those that have ranged abilities such as axes and Reapers.

This fight can be attempted at a lower gear level with patience if you stay at range the whole time. For that purpose, ranged abilities such as Sanguine Coil or Chaos Volley are ideal. Using spells with jewels that cleanse debuffs is also an excellent defensive option. Lastly, unholy spells that summon allies should be avoided as they will cause The Horror to use melee attacks much more often.

Scholar Blood is the ideal blood type for this fight as the bulk of your damage should be done via abilities, with another option being Brute Blood for it healing capabilities and +1 Gear Level. If you want extra burst survivability, go for Warrior Blood.

sections.title: The Fight
sections.body:
General Tips: As previously mentioned, keeping your distance is the best strategy for this fight. This is due to the fact that The Winged Horror's Swipe and Tail Whip should be avoided at all costs as well as The Winged Horror itself retreating if you attempt to get close. If you start burning, it is beneficial to get close to the icicles from The Horror's other attacks, such as it's spin, so that you stop taking continuous damage, the slow being rather negligible.

Unmentioned attacks: Aside from the Swipe and Tail Whip, all the unmentioned attacks have obvious circle markers where they damage the player. Thusly, there isn't much detail to go into. As for Swipe and Tail Whip, The Winged Horror should never be in range to perform these attacks.

Flare Charge: There is a small space between The Horror and it's fireballs where the player can stand to safely dodge the attack. That said, using your Travel Ability or other defensive abilities such as counters or barriers is a safe way of avoiding this attack. The ability used will most likely be available again by the time of the next charge as The Horror doesn't perform this attack often.

Fireball Volley 1: The player should be cautious while dodging this attack. While it is easier to dodge by keeping distance between you and The Horror, do not go too far back otherwise you'll find yourself on scorched earth. As for the attack itself, you can slip between the fireballs when they don't overlap, as well as dash through them or use a counter or barrier ability.

Fireball Volley 2: The gust of wind that knocks the player back is in a cone shape and the fireballs will only be shot in that cone. As such, it is possible to escape the cone, dodging all the fireballs in the process.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
*Swipe - Terrorclaw swipes in front of him, then slams forward, freezing.
*Charge - Terrorclaw roars, then leaps forward and bites.
*Slam - Terrorclaw slams the ground, creating three lines of ice. After a delay, icicles appear on the lines, freezing. Ice Block/Phantom Aegis can be used to MITIGATE the damage received if a dodge/side step is not an option for you or a teammate. 
*Roar - Terrorclaw roars, incapacitating nearby enemies.
*Icicles - Terrorclaw slams the ground multiple times, causing icicles to be dropped on the ground. These block most of his abilites.
*Throw ice - Terrorclaw picks up a icicle, then throws to the player stunning on hit. This projectile pierces icicles on the ground. Looks to be intercepting (aimed toward a location which would hit if the target kept moving in the same direction). This attack can be fully parried with abilities such as Blood Rite, abilities such as Ward Of The Damned will NOT work(Ward of the Damned appears to work as of the Gloomrot update).
*Freezing breath - Terrorclaw glows blue-white, then releases two waves in a large cone, freezing. The damage scales with proximity. This attack is blocked by icicles.
*Arctic leap - Terrorclaw leaps in the air, slamming down in a large area dealing AoE damage.
Upon landing, 4 novas of frost radiate out from the center, freezing.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
*Flaming strike - He coats his sword with fire and then swipes forward in an overhead swing after a short delay. This attack lights the player on fire if it hits them.
*Icy swing - He coats his sword with ice and then immediately sweeps it in a wide arc in front of him that inflicts . He often uses this as a follow-up attack after Flaming strike.
*Lunge - He leaps forward while thrusting his sword. This attack briefly snares the player if it hits them, but can be blocked by counter or shield abilities.
*Flaming Crossbow - He draws his crossbow and fires a flaming bolt at the player. If the bolt hits the player, a minion, or the environment it will detonate and light a large area of the ground on fire. If blocked by a shield spell or countered, the bolt will disappear without leaving a flame patch.
*Fire Bombs - He throws a fire bomb in the air which explodes into 5 separate bombs, lighting the ground on fire for several seconds when they land. He will often follow up this attack by firing his crossbow immediately afterwards.

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty
sections.body: *Whirlwind - Once Tristan reaches around 50% health, he shouts "Die... and stay dead!" and starts rapidly spinning with his sword, gaining movement speed and dealing massive damage in a large area around him and flipping players over his head if he hits them. This ability cannot be blocked by barrier spells (e.g.  or ) but its first hit can be blocked by counters (e.g. ). He can use this ability multiple times per fight.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
Tristan is an incredibly dangerous boss that can often prove difficult for players to defeat. Fighting him frequently results in the entire road being covered in fire, making it difficult to deal damage to him without being set aflame. It is highly recommended to bring a counter or barrier spell (such as  or ) to block his Flaming Crossbow attack and prevent even more of the area from being set on fire. For the same reason, it is also important to fight him in large areas that will be harder for him to fully cover with fire. Narrow roads and bridges should be avoided at all costs.

His massive AoE fire damage makes minion builds less viable as a source of damage, however they can still distract him and cause him to use deadly abilities on them instead of the player.  is incredibly effective at blocking his attacks while also creating such distractions. Failing that, Tristan is hostile to creatures and undead so luring him into a Treant, Stone Golem, or Corpse Pile can result in them fighting each other for a short time. 

Flaming strikes overheard swing can be sidestepped if the player sees it coming but Icy swings horizontal swing cannot.

Whirlwind is Tristan's most deadly attack on brutal difficulty, and can be very difficult to avoid unless the player is prepared for it. The best method to evading this attack is to fight Tristan near a large indestructible rock, tree, or pond that the player can kite him around until he finishes spinning. If this isn't an option then the player can Veil dash through Tristan to distract him with the afterimage, and then immediately shapeshift into wolf form and run away until his whirlwind effect expires. Tristan can also be distracted while using this attack and will waste it on local wildlife, undead, or summoned minions if they are closer to him than the player. His AI will sometimes become confused if a minion targeted by his whirlwind dies, and will waste the rest of its duration spinning on the location of the deceased minion.

sections.title: Location
sections.body:
Vincent can be found patrolling the central region of the [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=90 Dunley Farmlands], starting and ending in the 
[https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=90 Militia Encampment] just north of Haunted Iron Mine. His path proceeds southwest before turning north around the eastern side of Mosswick Village, heading to the northern roads of Dunley, then turning south past the eastern side of the Dunley Farmers Market to circle back to his starting point. He is guarded by two Militia Crossbowmen.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
*Double Swipe - His basic melee attack consists of 2 swipes with his mace that inflict .
*Frost Barrier - He creates a reflective shield that radiates a cone of frost damage which inflicts  if hit. The shield does not deflect AoE attacks such as  or the crossbow's Rain of Bolts.
*Crystal Lance - He holds his shield in the air, then swipes it in front of him, firing 5 ice projectiles in a cone that inflict . This ability is signaled by a distinct shrill sound effect.
*Chill Charge - He shouts "I feel a chill coming on!" and gains increased movement speed as well as ice particles around his feet. After running back and forth for a moment he will charge toward the player and inflict  if he hits them, then repeat this process 2 more times. 
*Ice Vortex - He holds his shield in the air and conjures a large vortex of ice around him that inflicts . After a brief delay the vortex detonates, dealing massive damage to players inside it. The explosion deals damage a little further than the area indicates and the damage cannot be blocked by counter or barrier spells but can be dodged with a Veil dash.

sections.title: Brutal Difficulty
sections.body:
Being in combat with him will cause the player to become snared (i.e. slowed) and lose 2 health per second. This health loss can be blocked by shields, such as those created by Frost Magic spells.
*Crystal Lance - This ability now fires 9 ice projectiles instead of 5.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
Vincent is an incredibly deadly boss that can easily lock players down with  while dealing massive damage to them. The threat of his freeze abilities means that using at least one defensive ability (such as a counter or shield spell) is highly encouraged to block them and prevent the player from being locked down. His Frost Barrier also makes minions (such as the skeletons from the Unholy spell tree) less desirable since they will often attack his shield and trigger the frost damage.

His Chill Charge is one of his most deadly abilities, since he can chain freeze the player or follow up with an Ice Vortex for massive damage. This attack can be dealt with by using a Veil dash at the last second to avoid it and hopefully trick him into using the 2nd charge on the player's afterimage. A barrier spell (such as  or ) can also block one or even 2 charges if he follows up very quickly. If all else fails then fighting him near a large physical obstacle, such as an indestructible rock, can allow the player to kite him around it while he wastes his charges.

As a member of the Militia, Vincent will be aided by any militia patrols or other allied V Blood bosses (such as Christina the Sun Priestess) who cross his path. This can make it difficult to fight him 1-on-1 while he is on patrol unless the player baits him away from the road or fights him at his Militia Encampment starting point after clearing it out ahead of time.

Alternatively, players can attempt to bait Vincent into fighting with Bane the Shadowblade if the two cross paths on their patrols through Dunley. One of them will likely kill the other while the survivor will be severely wounded and easier to finish off.

infobox.title: Voltatia the Power Master
infobox.location: [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=37 Trancendum Power Plant] in Gloomrot North
infobox.description: The trusted Right Hand of Doctor Henry Blackbrew, Voltatia is responsible for the maintenance and protection of the entire electric pipeline of Gloomrot, providing the region with their much needed energy supply. A stern professional and born leader, Voltatia operates with psychotic efficiency, and has little emotional desire beyond keeping The Doctor's operation running smoothly.

sections.title: Location
sections.body: Voltatia can be found in the [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=37 Trancendum Power Plant] in Gloomrot North.

sections.title: Phase 1 - (100%-81%)
sections.body:
*Electro Ray - This is her main attack, used in any proximity. Voltatia will stop and charge her cannon for 1.5s, after which she will track your position and fire for 2.5-3s. This attack is best side-stepped, ensure you're moving while she charges her cannon. Parry spells such as Blood Rite will not work not even for one tick, neither will shield spells such as Ward of the Damned, damage can however be mitigated with absorption spells such as Ice Block but cannot be fully absorbed without a top-tier spell power build. I recommend not wasting your dodge on this attack unless there's 2 Voltatias shooting from 2 very different angles. Rage spells such as Power Surge can help very much with its increased movement speed to easily side step this attack and do some damage. All dodge abilities such as Veil of Chaos will fool Voltatia to shoot the figure you leave behind, allowing you to throw a Vermin Salve or Blood Rose Brew down the gullet to keep 100% health during the first two less intense phases.

*Electro Shotgun - This is her preferred close proximity attack, she will morph her cannon in a wider nozzle for 1s and shoot once in a cone fashion multiple bullets. This attack has several counters. If you are in melee range then you could side step it by circling her if you do it right. The attack can be parried with spells such as Blood Rite, it can also be blocked with spells like Ward of the Damned, damage can be fully absorbed with Ice Block if you have spell power ~40, Phantom Aegis is weaker in strength, it will not fully absorb - you'll need spell power over 50 which is hard without a dedicated spell power build.

*Teleport - Voltatia will infuse with electricity and teleport to another location. You could use Polarity Shift if you want to stay close to her for melee damage, although keep in mind you have finite active spell slots, might not be worth it for your play style.

*Electric dome - Voltatia will generate a dome of electricity and turn invisible and run to reposition to attack you. If you are inside the dome, it will not cause any damage, it will simply push you a few steps back. The dome does not block projectiles. While doing this ability she becomes briefly immobile, creating an opportunity to use a spell like Void or Corrupted Skull for some extra damage

sections.title: Phase 2 - (80%-61%)
sections.body:
*Minion summon - She will stop and shout for help, summoning 2 Railgunners. They are comparatively weak, just keep them in mind and hit them when you can, they have static aim so they are easy to dodge, they will also make a mini-shotgun and blast you if you're too close and unlucky but it doesn't deal as much damage as Voltatias shotgun. Any offensive spell works against them as they move around a lot and long range hits will be a boon against them.

*Lightning curtain - she will place down a fence of electricity and stand behind it using her electro ray to deal damage. In this state she is static, therefore any target area spell such as Void can be used to summon damage right next to her. Projectile spells such as Chaos Volley will NOT work, it will be absorbed by the fence, even Chaos Barrage, an ultimate ability, can't get through. If you touch this barrier you will receive damage, the only way to get past this fence is to either walk around it or dash through it using your dodge to apply melee damage.

sections.title: Phase 3 - (60%-41%)
sections.body: *Clone - Voltatia will bash her weapon multiple times and phase out, after which 2 Voltatias will attack you for the remainder of the fight. Until now you've been fighting on easy mode, forget healing, forget using dash whenever you want, keep side stepping, keep using your spells to damage and use melee damage as you move better with melee, keep your main weapon and have the Sanguine Slashers on standby too - use the slashers ability Camouflage to turn invisible in order to reposition and try a different angle, especially if you're stuck in a bad position. try to keep your dodge as movement towards Voltatia and prioritise ending the battle quickly from now, I recommend using Veil of Chaos as it allows you to double dodge and get further. Hitting any Voltatia damages the other too, so hit any Voltatia you can. I also recommend using Potion of Rage and Witch Potion to increase your spell damage/shield and primary damage too.

sections.title: Phase 4 - (40%-0%)
sections.body: *Electro disc - Voltatia will lower herself and activate her back device which will throw ricocheting electric discs at you. This move is best countered with a combination of sidestepping, parry and dodge if it allows you to get near a Voltatia to damage her. For this move there is no one strategy which is better than the other, but dodging into the wave of discs to get to the Voltatia behind seems like the more favourable strategy because it allows you to go on the offensive instead of the defensive, so Veil of Chaos is best.

sections.title: Quotes
sections.body:
*"I have failed you, Doctor..." (Defeated)
*"But who, will take my place?" (Defeated)
*"My legs won't move!" (Defeated)

infobox.title: Willfred the Village Elder
infobox.description: An honored and deeply respected chief of a small, reclusive village of outcasts. Despite the imminent threat of the Cult of the Damned, dangerous wildlife, and even the rumor of Werewolves stalking northern Dunley, he manages to keep his people fed and happy.

sections.title: Location
sections.body:
Willfred can be found in the [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=52 Gracefall Village] located in the North-Eastern region of Dunley Farmlands, but can only be fought as Willfred the Werewolf Chief during nighttime.

During Daytime, Willfred reverts to human form, becoming Willfred the Village Elder, and dies if you kill him, preventing you from drinking his blood. If human form Willfred is killed, the normal V blood respawn timer will start.  It is not possible to try and fight Willfred at lower hp by damaging him during the day first; When Willfred transforms back into werewolf form, all HP is regained.

sections.title: Attacks
sections.body:
*Swipe - Willfred will swipe at you up to 2 times. This is extended if he hits both swipes, or cut short if you leave his range.
*Rage - Willfred glows red, walks towards you quickly, and bites at you 3 times in quick succession.
*Lunge - Willfred gets on all fours and prepares to lunge at you. This will inflict a 3 second stun and deal heavy damage as he shouts "Hold still".
*Heart Strike - Willfred will turn invisible and encircle his prey. On Brutal Difficulty, Willfred will also summon a Frost Wolf for every player in combat. When he reveals himself again, Willfred will lunge at you with an attack that inflicts the Heart Strike debuff, This explodes and deals damage after 3 seconds. This attack's application and explosion cannot be countered, only evadedIf an invulnerability effect is active when the effect expires, such as that from a successful counter or a dash, no damage will be taken. Occasionally Willfred will summon a copy of himself, which also performs Heart Strike once in close proximity. This appears to trigger randomly.Citation needed

When Willfred drops below 50% health for the first time, he'll howl and release a number of PrisonersLikely scaling with player count from the three cages around his 'arena'. When Willfred shouts "Let me have a taste" Willfred will try to eat one of them to restore his health. If Willfred successfully consumes a villager, Willfred will HealPotentially Exclusive to Brutal difficulty and  Rage - running at the player. It is advised to kill as many prisoners as you can before Willfred consumes them.

sections.title: Death
sections.body: "Gah... I am the top of a food chain... How could this be?.."

sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
Unlike other counters, Discharge can block an indefinite amount of attacks. Storm Shields last for 5s.

It was nerfed in 1.0 Hotfix #6 the following ways:
*Stun duration reduced to 0.6s from 0.8s.
*Jewel that allows you to recast, damage reduced from 25 - 50% to 15 - 30% and knockback effect power reduced by ~25%.
*Jewel increasing stun duration reduced from 0.2 - 0.4s to 0.1 - 0.3s.
*Jewel granting immaterial, duration reduced from 0.8 - 1.6s to 0.8 - 1.2s

It was nerfed further in the 1.1 Update the following ways:
* The immaterial jewel was removed. 
* Targets triggering the counter are no longer subjected to the stun or knockback effect if they're immaterial when the trigger happens. Static is still inflicted. 
* The recast jewel now inflicts a fading snare rather than knockback (no longer interrupting casts).

sections.title: History
sections.body:
Soulburn was added with the release of V Rising's first expansion, Secrets of Gloomrot on May 17th, 2023.
It was unlocked upon defeating Lord Styx the Night Champion.
It had a cooldown of , a cast time of , and the following effect:
{{Quote|Drain a life from up  nearby enemies dealing  magic damage, inflicting  and Leeching  health. Cancels any attack the enemy performs, silencing them for .|width=5px}}


The spell could instantly cancel almost all non-counter player spells and weapon skills. If none were cancelled immediately, a unique "Spell Block" debuff would automatically cancel the player's next spell or weapon skill cast for ~0.7s, including primary attacks. Only if something was cancelled would the silence trigger.
Over the years it was subjected to two nerfs:

In [https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1604030/view/3657533302488647084 Gloomrot Hotfix #7] its silence duration was nerfed from 2.5s to 1.5s. 

In Update 1.0 its cast time was nerfed from 0.2 to 0.5s.

Finally, in Update 1.1 it was reworked into its current iteration.

Soul Shard.png|category=Soul Shard|description=Place the Soul Shard in your Castle to utilise its power.|bloodbound=No|teleportable=No|salvageable=No|stack_size=1}}
This page is historical. It describes how Soul Shards used to function prior to Update 1.0. For the current accessories, see Soul Shards.

 were end tier items dropped by Shard Bearers. They could be planted in a player's territory like the current Shard Pedestals. Interacting with the Shard gave the player access to a powerful 2-hour buff.

Players carrying a shard in their inventory receive a debuff until they either drop it or place it in their castle; it can't be stored in containers. The debuff will prevent the player from using Vampire Powers, Mounts or utilize cave passages. Movement speed is also reduced by 15% and they take 25% increased damage.

===Usage===
To place the shard, the player needs to move the item to their action bar in their inventory and press the corresponding button, then they can place it on their territory. It can be moved and dismantled from the build menu just like other structures. Once placed in their territory the player can harness its powers indefinitely by interacting with it.

sections.title: Soul Shard Mechanics
sections.body:
Upon equipping the jewelry, the player's ultimate ability is replaced with :

"Become invulnerable and channel a Blood Storm for 3s, launching up to 25 homing blood bolts at nearby enemies. Each bolt deals 100% magic damage and inflicts . End with a powerful nova, dealing 300% magic damage and pushing enemies away."

In Update 1.1. players may replace the Soul Shard's ultimate ability freely.

The damage bonus to vampires applies to both players and enemies.

 increases movement speed, damage output, attack speed, and life leech by 15% for 6 seconds.

Soul Shards lose durability over time and can only be repaired by feeding on Primal Blood Souls during Tier 2 Rift Incursions. Each Primal Blood Soul consumed restores 750 durability, distributed between all shards in the player's inventory. If a Soul Shard is destroyed it returns to its V Blood Carrier, in this case Dracula.
After Update 1.1 its durability loss may now be sped up or disabled via the Server Settings.

They may be teleported outside of raid windows, and carried while in . (toggleable in settings)

On PvP servers Soul Shards are dropped on death, and can be stolen by other players. To prevent this, they may be stored in their respective pedestals; .

Soul Shards are automatically destroyed if not picked up from the ground within 60 minutes.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
Emery is collected by mining Emery Nodes in Oakveil Woodlands. It can also drop as loot there. It is notably abundant at the west side of [https://vrising.fandom.com/wiki/Map:Vardoran?marker=104 Venom Blades Bastion], below Dantos the Forgebinder's Forge.

Emery requires a Gear Level 23 (Dark Silver) weapon tier or higher to mine. If struck too quickly, the nodes will explode, dropping damaging clusters in a wide area.  This does not affect the total amount of Emery harvested from each node, however.

Emery Golems can be found disguised as unusually-shaped Emery deposits, turning hostile when attacked, and dropping Emery when destroyed.

sections.title: Initiating a Duel
sections.body:
To initiate a duel, simply place down the flag via the action bar or right clicking the banner in your Inventory.

Once an opposing player has accepted the duel by interacting with the banner, the contest will commence after a 5 second countdown.

A Death Vortex will form a perimeter around both players during the duel, damaging anyone venturing into it.

The  allows for more elaborate contests, along with fine control over team size, arena size, Death Vortex speed, etc.

sections.title: Mechanics
sections.body:
*The Throw Daggers description is slightly misleading. You will always have a minimum of one dagger to throw, even without waiting the full 1.1 second. In practice this make the actual cooldown closer to the listed 0.55 seconds. This also means deliberately only casting Throw Daggers at max stacks results in a significant DPS loss.
*Dagger stacks can be gained and expended freely during the Throw Dagger cast time. However, the dagger stack cooldown resets at the end of the Throw Dagger cast time.
**For example, if you were to start casting Throw Dagger immediately upon reaching 2 stacks, the 0.6+ seconds of stack regeneration gained during the cast animation will be lost once you run out of daggers to throw.
*Simply holding down the attack input for Throw Daggers will result in near zero stack regeneration loss and optimal DPS output by default, if no attack speed bonuses are applied.
**However, minimizing stack regeneration loss in-between other Weapon Skills and Spells is tricky. It requires precise timing of your dagger throw such that the last dagger stack is gained right as you're running out of daggers to throw. If you undershoot the timing, even more stack regeneration will be lost.
*Throw Dagger will only leave a dagger on the ground if it hits a target or solid object.
*Release Daggers can be animation cancelled at any point, and all daggers will still return to the player.
*The returning daggers from Release Daggers won't pierce solid objects.
*The player is invincible during the leap of Rain of Daggers.
*Its unique bursty combo design and its ability to gain additional daggers from the Release Daggers skill makes a calculation of the primary skill's DPS in isolation unreflective of its actual damage output. When optimized, this weapon has some of the highest damage potential in the game.

sections.title: Pistol Mechanics
sections.body:
*Much like other weapons, you can weave abilities in between your primary combo attacks.
But unlike other weapons, the pistols only have a significant cast time for the first attack in the combo.
This makes the final two shots able to be weaved in much more seamlessly than the first.
*In the 1.1 October patch Explosive Bullet's explosion damage was reduced to 115% from 125%, and Fan the Hammer was slightly reworked:
**Can now move at 35% speed while channeling the attack.
**Channeling duration reduced to 1.3s from 1.5s (increasing firing rate).
**Cone size reduced by ~50% making the spread less random.
**Reduced the knockback on bullet hit slightly.

sections.title: Mechanics
sections.body:
*A Thousand Spears has diminishing returns, stacking up to 10 times and making the target immune for up to 7s. A full attack may inflict 8 stacks. The recast does not inflict any stacks and is unaffected by the diminishing returns.
*A Thousand Spears was nerfed in the 1.1 October patch the following ways:
**Reduced the move distance when stepping forward during the cast to 1.25 from 2.
**Increased cooldown to 9s from 8s.
**Increased Thrust recast time to 0.3s from 0.25s.
